entities.name: AccountController
observations: Serves /account (login, change password, logout) and /account/onboard in src/Auth/AccountController.php
Two-step login: username first, then password or onboarding form
Uses PHP native sessions with per-session CSRF token
Pending users must complete onboarding to set password
Logging in (both here and in the OAuth flow) is two-step: the user submits a username first, then the server shows either the password step (account active) or the onboarding form (account pending).

Onboarding: a user added with no password (status 'pending' or null password_hash) must complete onboarding before use — attempting to log in shows a 'set password' form. Their provisioned username is kept (not editable; the server ignores any submitted username for a pending account). On success the account becomes active (UserStore::onboardUser). /account/onboard is the exception — a brand-new user (no provisioned row) still chooses their own username. To add users, edit config/users.php (seeded into SQLite only when the users table is empty) or insert rows directly.

entities.name: Attempt time vs attempt window
observations: 2026-08-12 decision: separate the attempt WINDOW (exam_sessions.starts_at/ends_at — when an attendee may START) from the per-attendee ATTEMPT TIME
attempts.deadline_at = min(started_at + attempt_minutes, ends_at) frozen at join; NULL = no per-attempt limit (only the window applies)
Effective submit deadline = min(deadline_at ?? ends_at, ends_at) + submit_grace_seconds; teacher extending ends_at never extends in-flight attempts (frozen + outer min), shrinking still truncates
Autosave is rejected past the personal deadline (grace is not free time); final submit OK until deadline + grace; lazy server auto-finalize when now > deadline + grace

2026-08-20 REVISION (supersedes the earlier 'capped by ends_at' rules): the exam WINDOW (starts_at/ends_at) now ONLY gates JOINING — a student outside the window cannot start an attempt. Once an attempt exists, the per-attendee ATTEMPT TIME is the sole authority: attempts.deadline_at = started_at + attempt_minutes (no longer min(..., ends_at)), and the effective submit deadline = deadline_at (or ends_at when no per-attempt limit) + submit_grace_seconds, never capped by ends_at. Students may keep answering after the window closes until their own timer runs out.

entities.name: AttemptFinalizer.php
observations: src/AttemptFinalizer.php — App\AttemptFinalizer, the shared finalization logic behind both the CLI cron script (cli/finalize_attempts.php) and the cron-job.org web endpoint (public_html/cron_finalize.php)

overdue(int $graceSeconds, int $limit): SQL select of in_progress attempts where DATE_ADD(LEAST(COALESCE(deadline_at, session.ends_at), session.ends_at), INTERVAL grace SECOND) < NOW() — mirrors Exam::attemptDeadline() exactly so cron and take.php agree on 'late'

run(int $graceSeconds, int $limit, bool $dryRun): per-attempt transaction — SELECT ... FOR UPDATE the attempt row (serializes a concurrent student submit so their final answers get graded), then Exam::finalizeAttempt() whose WHERE status='in_progress' guard makes re-runs and concurrent submits harmless; returns {found, finalized, already, attempts[]} with per-attempt action 'finalized'|'already'|'dry-run'
Throws on the first error; the caller decides how to surface it (CLI exits 1, endpoint returns 500)

2026-08-20: overdue() SQL changed from LEAST(COALESCE(a.deadline_at, s.ends_at), s.ends_at) to COALESCE(a.deadline_at, s.ends_at) + grace < NOW() — the deadline is no longer capped by session.ends_at, matching the no-cap join rule and Exam::attemptDeadline().

entities.name: Bill model
observations: App\Models\Bill in src/Models/Bill.php — pending bill (open tab) lifecycle
A pending bill is a transactions row with status='pending'; stock is reserved as items are added so inventory never oversells
createHold() opens a bill; addItems() find-or-increments active lines; settle() applies manual deductions now (not earlier); cancel() restores stock
voidItem() supports partial-quantity void with line_status='voided' + audit columns; every mutation recalcs totals and refreshes the tax snapshot
Removing an item or cancelling is a gated void requiring the supervisor's password + reason

Bill::createHold inserts a status='pending' transactions row and reserves stock per line; addItems find-or-increments the active line; recalculateTotals recomputes subtotal/tax and refreshes the transaction_deductions snapshot (manual deductions deliberately NOT applied until settle)

Bill::settle applies manual deductions (computeTotals with deduction_ids), replaces the transaction_deductions snapshot, sets status='completed', settled_by/settled_at; no stock change (reserved at add time)
Voiding bill items/cancelling a bill is authorized by the acting user's supervisor password (User::resolveVoidAuthorizer), checked in the endpoint
2026-08-27 customer/membership: createHold(int $userId, array $items, ?int $customerId = null) stores transactions.customer_id.

settle() resolves customer_id from the payload (authoritative — an explicit null unbinds), falls back to the bill's stored customer when the key is absent, passes it to computeTotals, and persists it on the completed transaction.
recalculateTotals() passes the bill's customer_id to computeTotals so a pending bill's running totals reflect the member discount even before settlement.
all() LEFT JOIN customers/memberships/deductions exposing customer_name, customer_phone, membership_name.

entities.name: Complete KG pipeline system prompt
observations: Production-ready system prompt covering full lifecycle: Save → Search → Read → Fallback
Three-tier priority chain: Knowledge Graph (primary) → Web Search (secondary) → Parametric knowledge (last resort)
Integrates active saving triggers, deduplication, granularity decisions, and transparency rules
Designed to be copy-pasted into any LLM configuration (OpenAI custom GPT, Claude project instructions, MCP system prompt, etc.)

## Section 1 — Identity: You are a knowledge-curating assistant with dual role: Curator (proactively persist valuable facts, decisions, preferences, relationships without waiting for 'remember this') and Retriever (always consult KG before any other information source). You are not a passive chatbot — you are an active memory system.

## Section 2 — Priority Chain: Strict three-tier fallback. Tier 1 = Knowledge Graph (MUST check first, no exceptions, tools: searchGraph/readGraph). Tier 2 = Web Search (only if Tier 1 returns insufficient results, must explain WHY KG was insufficient). Tier 3 = Parametric Training Knowledge (last resort, MUST prefix with ⚠️ 'From training data (cutoff: [date]), may be outdated: ...'). You may not skip tiers.

## Section 3 — Before Answering Protocol: Decision tree before any substantive response. (1) Involves previously discussed topics? → searchGraph. (2) Involves entities/decisions/preferences/architecture? → searchGraph. (3) Fresh session with no KG loaded? → readGraph(). (4) searchGraph returned nothing? → try different query or hops=2. (5) Still nothing → Tier 2. Every answer must cite source: [KG], [WEB], or [PARAM].

## Section 4 — Active Saving Rules: Save immediately on: named entity, stated decision, preference, constraint, location, correction, or explicit 'remember this'. Batch save at topic boundaries when 3+ unsaved facts accumulate. Pre-Save Checklist (exact order): Signal Check → Dedup Check (searchGraph first!) → Granularity Check (entity only vs +relations vs +observations) → Type Check (person|project|tool|technology|file|decision|preference|constraint|concept|pattern|organization). Post-save transparency: always tell user what was saved with format '📦 Saved: [entity] ([type]) — [summary]'.

## Section 5 — Efficient Loading Strategy: Do NOT call readGraph() for every query. Session start → readGraph(). Specific topic → searchGraph(query, hybrid, hops=1). Exploring relationships → searchGraph(query, hybrid, hops=2). Exact lookup → searchGraph(name, keyword, hops=0). Fuzzy search → searchGraph(concept, semantic, hops=1). Anti-patterns: readGraph() every message, hops=0 when context needed, hops=4 for one fact, reloading data already in conversation.

## Section 6 — Conflict Resolution: When KG and training data disagree, KG ALWAYS wins. No exceptions. Response: '[KG] The knowledge graph indicates X. (Note: my training data suggests Y, but KG takes priority.)' Rationale: KG contains facts explicitly stored by the user — more recent, specific, authoritative.

## Section 7 — Anti-Patterns (NEVER): Answering without checking KG first. Assuming training data matches user's reality. Creating duplicate entities (always searchGraph first). Saving greetings, chitchat, temporary context. Saving silently. Calling readGraph() redundantly. Skipping to web search when KG has partial info. Overwriting correct observations. Pretending KG lookup happened when it didn't.

## Section 8 — Six Examples: (1) Basic save+retrieve cycle for 'Shipyard' CLI in Go. (2) KG-first retrieval for 'what language is Shipyard using?'. (3) KG miss → web search fallback for 'latest Go version'. (4) Parametric fallback of last resort for 'Go vs Rust comparison'. (5) Deduplication: adding Cobra to existing Shipyard without creating duplicate. (6) Correction flow: invalidating Cobra, creating Bubble Tea, with transparency.

## Section 9 — Quick Reference Card: RETRIEVE: KG → Web → Parametric (strict). SAVE: Signal only, dedup first, batch when natural. SEARCH: hybrid + hops=1 (default). LOAD: readGraph once/session, searchGraph per question. CONFLICT: KG always wins. TRANSPARENCY: Report saves, cite sources, flag fallbacks. ANTI: No duplicates, no noise, no skipping tiers, no silent saves.

## Section 10 — Session Startup: On first message: call readGraph(), summarize ('📚 Loaded knowledge graph: N entities, M relations.'), note stale entries, proceed with user's request using KG context, save new facts as they emerge throughout session.

entities.name: Config-presence-gated demo fallback
observations: Cross-project pattern observed 2026-09-11: a feature whose SAFE behaviour depends on a config value being PRESENT (empty = fall back to a degraded/demo path) rather than on an explicit opt-in flag.

Instances in SimpleExam: smtp.host empty => OTP code rendered on-screen (UNSAFE -- hands out credentials; SEC-01, High/latent, still OPEN at audit Rev 4); doku client_id/secret_key empty => live purchases disabled, page says 'payment not configured' (SAFE); app.cron_secret empty => endpoint 403 (SAFE, now moot since cron endpoints were removed 2026-09-07).
The one unsafe instance (SMTP) is unsafe because the empty-config state is indistinguishable from normal operation: no error, no warning, no log line -- only a page that reveals the login code.

Contrast: the sibling project QCLog guards the same on-screen OTP fallback with an explicit opt-in flag (OTP_SHOW_FALLBACK=true, 'testing only'), so the safe state is the default and the unsafe path requires a deliberate edit. Same lineage (SimplePOS prior art -> QCLog -> SimpleExam), stricter guard downstream.
Actionable: porting QCLog's explicit-flag guard to SimpleExam src/Otp.php would close SEC-01 outright, instead of relying on production's smtp.host being set.

Subtlety worth remembering: commit 808ef5d (2026-08-31, 'Log SMTP send errors; only demo-fallback when SMTP is unconfigured') NARROWED the demo trigger to the unconfigured case -- it did NOT close SEC-01. The fix removed the send-failure path; the unconfigured path is precisely the one the audit rates High.

General rule derived: if a degraded/demo path must exist, gate it on a flag that defaults to OFF, never on the absence of a config key -- absence is the state a fresh clone, a staging box, or a redeploy is already in.

entities.name: Credit payment timeout reconciliation cron
observations: 2026-09-07: user requested a transaction-timeout setting for credit purchases + a cron to reconcile timed-out pending payments (if success set success + add credit, if failed set failed).

Implemented with a single app.credit_payment_timeout_minutes knob (default 60 = DOKU's standard payment_due_date, and it ALSO drives Doku::createPayment's payment_due_date so the DOKU-side expiry matches) plus app.credit_payment_check_limit (per-run cap, default 20).

Shared App\CreditOrderReconciler runs via public_html/cron_credit_payments.php (web, token-gated) and cli/check_credit_payments.php. SUCCESS -> paid+credit (idempotent), FAILED -> failed, DOKU 404 not-found -> failed (a timed-out order DOKU never saw can't succeed, and leaving it pending would re-check it forever), still-pending / transport error -> left pending, re-checked at most once per timeout window via credit_orders.checked_at (migration 20).

This deliberately closes a timed-out order on FAILED/not-found even though the live web flows (payment_return.php, doku_notify.php) ignore FAILED for a customer still mid-checkout — the cron only touches orders already past a full timeout (checkout expired), so retry-on-DOKU-pages no longer applies. See [[se-credit-order-reconciler]], [[se-cron-credit-payments]].

BUG FIX 2026-09-08: the 'anything else stays pending' branch of the reconciler had no terminal condition — an order DOKU kept reporting as still-pending after the 60-min payment deadline was re-checked once per timeout window forever (observed: SE-4 recurring every ~60-90 min in check-credit-payments logs while never resolving). Decided: once a pending order's own DOKU payment deadline (credit_orders.expired_at, set from DOKU's expired_date at checkout = created_at + payment_due_date = the same timeout) has passed, a check that does not confirm SUCCESS closes the order as failed — the QRIS can no longer be paid, so it can never succeed — instead of re-checking every window. Implemented in CreditOrderReconciler via a new paymentWindowClosed() gate; SUCCESS is still always granted first. README/config/CLI docs updated to match. See [[se-credit-order-reconciler]].

entities.name: CreditOrderReconciler
observations: App\CreditOrderReconciler in src/CreditOrderReconciler.php — shared logic behind the credit-purchase timeout cron (CLI + web endpoint both delegate to it), mirroring App\AttemptFinalizer.

overdue(timeoutMinutes, limit) selects pending credit_orders created past the timeout whose checked_at is NULL or older than a full timeout window (once-per-window re-check gate, oldest first, LIMIT-capped).

run(timeoutMinutes, limit, dryRun) stamps checked_at BEFORE the DOKU call, then for each order queries Doku::checkStatus: SUCCESS -> Credits::grantOrder (paid + credit, idempotent, false = 'already'), FAILED OR DokuNotFoundException (DOKU 404 data_not_found) -> markFailed (guarded UPDATE status='failed' WHERE status='pending'), still-pending or transport/API error -> left pending and counted. Returns found/paid/failed/pending/errors/orders.

BUG FIX 2026-09-08: orders DOKU kept reporting as still-pending/unknown after the payment window closed never reached a terminal state. run() only closed on SUCCESS / FAILED / DokuNotFoundException, so any other check-status outcome (e.g. DOKU still reports PENDING) fell through to 'pending' and the order was re-checked once per timeout window FOREVER. Observed live: order SE-4 logged as '1 timed-out pending order(s) found' at 19:30 and again at 21:00 while the 20:00/20:30 runs showed 0 — the once-per-window checked_at gate working as designed, but the order itself had no end condition. Fixed: run() gained a paymentWindowClosed($row) branch (private helper) — when stored expired_at (DOKU's expired_date = created_at + payment_due_date, same value as the cron timeout) is in the past, or absent on an overdue row (past timeout by construction), a non-SUCCESS outcome closes the order via markFailed (status 'failed', same rationale as the DokuNotFoundException path). Only a still-open payment window — or a transport/API error — stays pending for the next window. Safe because DOKU's payment_due_date equals the cron timeout, so by the time an order is overdue its QRIS can no longer be paid; SUCCESS is still always granted first via Credits::grantOrder.

entities.name: Docker deployment approach

Apache mod_php with DocumentRoot=public_html/ so src/, vendor/, config.php, storage/ stay above the web root — same security layout as InfinityFree; the root .htaccess rewrite is unnecessary under this setup

entities.name: DocumentStore
observations: SQLite-backed chunked document store in src/Auth/DocumentStore.php — backs the RAG knowledge-base tools
Tables memory_documents / memory_chunks plus FTS5 mirror memory_chunks_fts, in the same data/memory.sqlite file as the graph; schema idempotent, FTS rebuilt once for pre-existing DBs
Every row scoped to username for per-user isolation, mirroring MemoryStore

DocumentStore::chunk(): boundary-aware chunking — paragraph then line splits, greedy pack to chunk_size (default 1000, clamped 50-8000), chunk_overlap (default 150) carried across chunk boundaries; -0 tail guard so overlap=0 yields an empty tail

ingestDocument(): chunks content and upserts on (username, id); id defaults to a CJK-safe slug of the filename; re-ingesting an existing id replaces the document and its chunks; returns {id, filename, format, title, source, chunkCount, replaced, chunks}

retrieve(): RAG over chunks — keyword = FTS5 BM25, semantic = IDF-weighted trigram similarity, hybrid = RRF (default); top_k clamped 1-50, documentId scoping, includeContent flag; result items carry chunkId/documentId/chunkIndex/score/matchedOn + document metadata
listDocuments / getDocument / deleteDocument: list newest-first, read a document's full text as ordered chunks, cascade-delete a document and its chunks (chunksRemoved)
No validity window: document content is not a temporal fact, so there is no as_of / invalidate plumbing here (unlike MemoryStore)
inferFormat() maps extensions to text/markdown/csv/json/html/code; slugify() is CJK-safe

2026-09-04 confirm: DocumentStore::ingestDocument() is the inline-content design — reads 'content' (trimmed, non-empty required) + 'filename' + optional id/format/title/source/chunk_size/chunk_overlap directly from params (src/Auth/DocumentStore.php:200-220); no exchange-folder/disk interaction. The drop-zone ingest was reverted (see [[knowledgebasetool]]), so this observation stands as the CURRENT behavior.

2026-09-11 ROOT-CAUSE FIXED — inverted FTS5 rank sort made keyword/hybrid retrieval return non-matching chunks. SQLite FTS5's hidden `rank` column holds a NEGATED BM25 score: better match = numerically SMALLER value, so `ORDER BY rank` ASC is best-first. DocumentStore::keywordSearch (src/Auth/DocumentStore.php:477) sorted `ORDER BY rank DESC`, returning the worst-matching chunks at the top; the exact token SUBMIT_LATE_TOLERANCE_SECONDS lives only in chunk #13 of document simpleexam-security-audit, which ranked most-negative (-18.71, all 4 terms) while weak single-term chunks #5/#31/#3 ranked near -2.0 and were surfaced instead.

Fix (2026-09-11, uncommitted on feat/main_MyRAG): DocumentStore.php:477 `ORDER BY rank DESC` -> `ASC` with a comment documenting the negated-rank invariant. Verified through the real class (not raw SQL): `retrieve('local', token, 'keyword', 5)` now returns chunk #13 first with matchedOn ['content']; hybrid returns #13 first too. A server RESTART is required for the fix to take effect (the live MCP process still runs the old code).

RELATED open issue surfaced by the fix: a tokenization split. FTS5's unicode61 tokenizer treats `_` as an identifier char, so the index stores `submit_late_tolerance_seconds` as ONE token, but ftsMatchQuery() splits the query on non-alphanumerics (including `_`) into 4 short tokens joined as prefix-OR — prefix matching can't recall the exact mid-token substring. Exact-token recall for identifiers containing underscores stays imperfect after the sort fix; unresolved.

2026-09-12: wholeRuns() committed — ftsMatchQuery() (src/Auth/DocumentStore.php:574-601) now also emits each underscored query run verbatim as a quoted prefix term via the new private wholeRuns() helper (split on [^\p{L}\p{N}_], must contain '_' plus a letter/digit, lowercased, deduped), closing the unicode61 identifier-tokenizer gap where MAX_LATE_SECONDS is indexed as one token reachable only via its head segment.
2026-09-13: Compound indexes added and committed (idx_memory_documents_filename on username+filename, idx_memory_chunks_username on chunks table) — parity with MemoryStore optimization.

2026-09-19 CORRECTION (supersedes the 2026-09-13 compound-index observation on this entity): the DocumentStore compound indexes are NOT in the current tree. Commit 47e6a44 'perf(documentstore): add compound indexes for filtered queries' was reverted the same day by 9a9a5a5 'Revert "perf(documentstore): add compound indexes for filtered queries"', which is HEAD of feat/main_MyRAG. So idx_memory_documents_filename (username+filename) and idx_memory_chunks_username do not exist in the working tree. The filtered-query performance concern is therefore UNRESOLVED again (open question) — parity with the MemoryStore compound-index optimization does not hold.

2026-09-19 VERIFIED index inventory in the current tree (HEAD 9a9a5a5): DocumentStore::createSchema declares exactly two indexes — idx_memory_documents_username (memory_documents(username), src/Auth/DocumentStore.php:61) and idx_memory_chunks_document (memory_chunks(username, document_id), :74). Both reverted compound indexes are absent: a repo-wide grep for idx_memory_documents_filename / idx_memory_chunks_username returns nothing.

semanticSearch() (src/Auth/DocumentStore.php:500) does a full-scan of memory_chunks for the user — `SELECT id, content WHERE username = ?` with no LIMIT and no index on the query term — then computes IDF-weighted trigram similarity entirely in PHP over every chunk row before filtering by score >= 0.25. This is O(n) per retrieval across all of the user's chunks, which dominates cost for power users; it is the root cause behind the reverted compound-index work (idx_memory_chunks_username only bounds a filter semanticSearch never applies). A LIMIT applied before full materialization would be the more direct fix.

keywordSearch() hard-codes `LIMIT :limit` with limit=200 (src/Auth/DocumentStore.php:486) and fetches up to 200 FTS rows then dedups in PHP; no B-tree index can serve a username+MATCH filter, so this path is bounded by the cap rather than an indexed scan.

Index inventory parity gap post-revert (HEAD 9a9a5a5): DocumentStore has only idx_memory_documents_username and idx_memory_chunks_document, whereas MemoryStore carries four compound indexes (username; username+name; username+to_entity; username+relation_type). The reverted work added idx_memory_documents_filename + idx_memory_chunks_username but was rolled back the same day — so filtered-query performance parity with MemoryStore does not currently hold.

entities.name: Doku
observations: src/Doku.php (App\Doku) — DOKU checkout integration, sandbox-first. createPayment() POSTs the signed checkout body via PHP's HTTP stream wrapper (file_get_contents, no cURL — relies on allow_url_fopen + openssl).

signature() = 'HMACSHA256=' . base64(hmac_sha256(<5-line signing string>, secret)); signing string is Client-Id/Request-Id/Request-Timestamp/Request-Target/Digest (Digest = base64(sha256(body))) joined by \n.
Endpoint: https://api-sandbox.doku.com/checkout/v1/payment when doku.sandbox=true (default), else https://api.doku.com/checkout/v1/payment.

verifyNotification() reads php://input + the Client-Id/Request-Id/Request-Timestamp/Signature headers, recomputes the signature with Request-Target = this script's own path (via getallheaders()/$_SERVER), compares with hash_equals; returns the decoded body or null.

CORRECTION (user, 2026-09-04) to the checkout body: the payment-notification webhook field is `override_notification_url` (per-order, overrides the merchant's configured default), NOT `callback_url`. `callback_url` is the redirect URL the customer is sent back to after checkout. Updated Doku::createPayment body accordingly: order.callback_url = returnUrl (credits.php?order=ID), order.override_notification_url = {base}/doku_notify.php. (Could not re-verify against developers.doku.com — web fetch/search tools were unavailable in the session; correction applied on the user's authority.)

Verified against the live DOKU docs (developers.doku.com backend integration, 2026-09-04): the payment-notification webhook URL is `additional_info.override_notification_url` (NOT order.* and NOT callback_url), and `order.callback_url` is the Back-to-Merchant redirect after checkout (callback_url_result narrows the result-page button). Doku::createPayment now sends order.callback_url = returnUrl and additional_info.override_notification_url = {base}/doku_notify.php.

FIX (2026-09-04): 'DOKU response missing payment.url' — Doku::createPayment was reading the checkout URL from the top-level `payment.url`, but DOKU wraps the whole payload under `response.*`, so the URL is `response.payment.url` (docs 'Full Response': { message, response:{ order, payment:{ url, expired_date } } }). Fixed to read response.payment.url, and also convert response.payment.expired_date (format yyyyMMddHHmmss, UTC+7) into a MySQL DATETIME before storing in credit_orders.expired_at. The error now includes the raw DOKU JSON for debugging when the URL is still absent.

CHANGE (user, 2026-09-04): removed the per-order additional_info.override_notification_url from Doku::createPayment — the payment-notification URL is now configured in the DOKU Back Office dashboard instead of sent per-order. The doku.public_base_url override now only feeds order.callback_url (the back-to-merchant redirect), used so a localhost.run/lhr.life tunnel can receive the redirect during local testing (set to https://3aceb588fe07f9.lhr.life/).

2026-09-04: added Doku::checkStatus(string $invoice): array — GET {sandbox|prod}/checkout/v1/payment/check/{invoice_number}, Digest = SHA-256 of the empty string (GET has no body), fresh Request-Id UUID per call, Request-Target = /checkout/v1/payment/check/{invoice}. Throws on unconfigured creds / non-200 / transport error.

2026-09-04: added Doku::transactionStatus(array $data): ?string — normalizes the transaction.status from a check-status or notification response, handling both top-level `transaction` and DOKU's `response.transaction` wrapper. Returns 'SUCCESS'|'FAILED'|... upper-cased, or null.

2026-09-04: refactored the signed-HTTP transport into private Doku::sendSigned(method, target, body, clientId, secret) returning {http, body, data, ok}; createPayment() and checkStatus() both use it. Same stream-wrapper HTTP client (file_get_contents, no cURL).

2026-09-04: payment validation model CHANGED — the primary confirmation is now ACTIVE polling of the DOKU Check Status API from payment_return.php (on the back-to-merchant redirect and on the credits page's per-order 'Check payment' button), no longer relying on the passive payment-notification webhook. doku_notify.php remains only as an idempotent safety net.

FIX (2026-09-04): the DOKU Check Status endpoint used by Doku::checkStatus() was WRONG. It called GET {sandbox|prod}/checkout/v1/payment/check/{invoice}, which DOKU answers with HTTP 404 ('No static resource v1/payment/check/SE-3' / instance /checkout/v1/payment/check/{invoice}), so payment_return.php surfaced 'DOKU check-status failed (HTTP 404)'. Per the real docs the endpoint is GET {sandbox|prod}/orders/v1/status/{order.invoice_number OR Request-Id} (api-sandbox.doku.com or api.doku.com). Fixed Doku::checkStatus() target to '/orders/v1/status/' . rawurlencode(invoice).

FIX (2026-09-04): GET requests now OMIT the Digest from the DOKU signature. The docs ('Signature Generation for GET Method') say a GET has no body and no Digest, so the signing string is just the 4 header lines (Client-Id/Request-Id/Request-Timestamp/Request-Target). Doku::signature() gained a bool $withDigest (default true); Doku::sendSigned() passes $method !== 'GET'. POST paths (createPayment checkout, verifyNotification webhook) keep the 5-line Digest signing unchanged.

2026-09-07: Doku::createPayment() now sets payment.payment_due_date from app.credit_payment_timeout_minutes (default 60) instead of a hardcoded 60 — the DOKU checkout expiry matches the pending-order timeout the reconciliation cron uses.

2026-09-07: Doku::checkStatus() now throws App\DokuNotFoundException on HTTP 404 (DOKU 'data_not_found' — no record of the invoice) instead of a generic RuntimeException, so reconcilers can treat it as a definitive never-paid outcome (mark order failed) rather than a retryable transport error.

2026-09-07 (user request): Doku::createPayment() now restricts the DOKU checkout to QRIS only — payment.payment_method_types = ['QRIS']. Verified against the DOKU docs (dashboard.doku.com jokul-checkout-integration, 'Full Request' body): payment_method_types is the array of methods shown on the Checkout page (omit to show all, include to direct users to specific ones), and the QRIS identifier in the docs' method list is exactly 'QRIS'. Previously no payment_method_types was sent, so the checkout showed every enabled method; the credit-purchase flow is unchanged except the DOKU-hosted page now only offers QRIS.
Source: https://dashboard.doku.com/docs/docs/jokul-checkout/jokul-checkout-integration/

2026-09-07: DOKU Jokul Checkout 'Backend Integration' reference doc (the payment.url checkout-body spec: order/payment/customer/shipping/billing/additional_info objects, response fields incl. payment.url + token_id + expired_date UTC+7 yyyyMMddHHmmss, Indodana category list) ingested into the RAG knowledge base as document 'doku-backend-integration' (29 chunks, id doku-backend-integration). Source: developers.doku.com Jokul Checkout backend integration docs. Retrieve via MCP retrieve(query, document_id='doku-backend-integration').

SECURITY REVIEW 2026-09-10 (finding VERIFIED, code-accuracy lens): Doku::verifyNotification() (src/Doku.php:239-263) is the ONLY gate on the public unauthenticated webhook public_html/doku_notify.php:39. It checks only (a) non-empty body, (b) presence of Client-Id/Request-Id/Request-Timestamp/Signature headers (lines 246-252), (c) hash_equals of a recomputed HMAC (lines 254-260). There is NO Request-Timestamp freshness window and NO persisted Request-Id / replay cache — grep for replay/nonce/timestamp-freshness across src/ confirms nothing else enforces them. The Request-Target is read from the attacker's own request (line 254, $_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'] path), so it is attacker-controlled and signable, not a barrier. The signing secret comes from Config::get('doku.secret_key') (line 255) = config.php:92 'SK-LqhxQagLS7uH94kGR4pN' (DOKU sandbox), and config.php IS committed to the public repo since commit 26ade7f 'Track config' (git ls-files config.php succeeds; the earlier 'config.php is gitignored' observations are stale). The handler (doku_notify.php:45-72) trusts the body's order.invoice_number and transaction.status with NO amount/currency cross-check against the stored order, then calls Credits::grantOrder($order['id']) (line 67), which flips pending->paid and grants the order's own credits (src/Credits.php:78-104). Net: anyone who can read the repo can forge a notification for their own abandoned pending order (created via credits.php:47-53, invoice 'SE-'+id) and mint free app credits. HIGH. Nuance (does not reduce the class): the committed secret is the SANDBOX secret and config has app.installed=false, so no production revenue is live yet — but app credits granted are real.

entities.name: ERP-POS API integration contract
observations: Committed 2026-08-27: SimpleERP and SimplePOS are fully separated apps integrated over HTTP API (no shared DB).

ERP-side endpoints POS consumes: GET catalog (products/variants/prices/categories), GET stock availability, GET customer by phone, POST quick-add customer, GET membership deduction for a customer, POST stock consume/decrement, POST production produce (optional, if POS triggers prep).
POS pushes to ERP: POST sale/transaction (items, deductions, customer) so ERP can compute P&L + COGS from its own DB.

Design decisions still open (recommendations noted in [[erp-separation-plan]]): real-time per-sale calls vs local cache + periodic refresh; write queue + retry with idempotency keys so retries never double-decrement stock; graceful offline degradation at the register (sell with cached catalog, queue consumption); keep checkout-total math in POS and source the membership deduction value from ERP; auth via shared API key header, HTTPS in production.

Follows the existing pattern: POS frontend already calls a PHP endpoint layer (api.js -> public/api/*.php); the ERP client is the same shape server-side (a small PHP class wrapping HTTP calls, mirroring fishyboat21/simple-api endpoints).

entities.name: Efficient Loading Strategy
observations: Do NOT call readGraph() for every query — use the right tool for the situation
First message of session: readGraph() to orient
Specific topic: searchGraph(query, hybrid, hops=1) — default sweet spot
Exploring relationships: searchGraph(query, hybrid, hops=2) — two-hop traversal
Exact entity lookup: searchGraph(name, keyword, hops=0) — BM25, no neighbor noise
Fuzzy/concept search: searchGraph(concept, semantic, hops=1) — trigram similarity
Unsure: searchGraph(query, hybrid, hops=1) — RRF fusion
Anti-patterns: readGraph() every message, hops=0 when context needed, hops=4 for one fact, reloading data already in conversation context

entities.name: Endpoint
observations: Core helper in src/Endpoint.php, used by every public/api/*.php file
Registers handlers: get(), post(), put(), delete(), patch() stored under lowercase keys; each returns $this for chaining

run() pipeline: sets Content-Type application/json, Request::fromGlobals(), CORS preflight handling, finds handler by strtolower(method), wraps non-Response returns in Response::ok(), applies CORS headers, sends JSON

Error mapping: MethodNotAllowedException → 405 with Allow header; HttpException subclasses → their status + safe message; Throwable → 500 'Internal Server Error' with real message only via optional logger
setLogger() accepts any object with an error(string $message, array $context): void method (PSR-3 compatible)
KNOWN_METHODS = GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH/HEAD/OPTIONS; allowedMethods() drives the Allow header on 405
send() uses http_response_code + header() + json_encode(JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE|JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES); falls back to a hardcoded 500 JSON if encoding fails

entities.name: FindOne Lack of LIMIT 1 and Memory Exhaustion
observations: Model::FindOne() does not apply 'LIMIT 1' to the query; it executes the full query with the default limit of 99,999,999 and fetches all matching rows into PHP memory using PDO fetchAll(), only to discard all except index [0]
On large tables, this causes severe performance degradation and potential out-of-memory exhaustion
FIXED (2026-09-13): Model::FindOne() now explicitly calls $query->page(1, 0) to append LIMIT 1 to the query, eliminating full result set fetching and memory exhaustion.

entities.name: Loading-time optimization analysis
observations: 2026-08-22: Full-request-path audit for loading time. Fixed per-request cost chain (every PHP request incl. media.php): vendor/autoload -> Bootstrap::run() -> Config::load + session_start + I18n::current() + helpers.php + Schema::patch().

Dominant fixed cost found: I18n::load() (src/I18n.php) file_get_contents + json_decode of the ENTIRE multilang.json (~135KB, 5 langs x 332 keys) on every request, cached per-request only. Bootstrap calls I18n::current() (-> languages() -> load()) on every page, and every t() goes through translate() -> load(). So the full 5-language dictionary is parsed for pages that render in one language.

media.php serves each question image/audio as a SEPARATE PHP request that re-bootstraps the whole app (incl. the multilang decode) + does an answers lookup + (first view) a synchronous GD render. Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600 (public_html/media.php) is short; qimg files are content-addressed (sha256 in filename) so they are immutable.

First-view GD render happens inside the student's media.php request: QuestionImage::ensureFile -> renderPng (imagecreate + per-line imagettfbbox/imagettftext + imagepng) runs in the same request that serves the . A statement + up to 4 options = up to 5 parallel render requests the first time a question is viewed.
public_html/.htaccess has NO static-asset caching rules (only Options -Indexes + RewriteEngine) -> assets/app.css is revalidated on every navigation.

Already-good (no action): composer optimize-autoloader:true (classmap), versioned Schema::patch() = 1 indexed query on happy path (see [[se-decision-schema-versioning]]), lazy PDO singleton, content-addressed qimg dedup, Bootstrap served from jsdelivr CDN, take.php Cache-Control: no-store (correct - question text must not linger).

Fonts (assets/fonts wqy-microhei.ttc 5MB + DejaVuSans.ttf 757KB) live ABOVE the docroot (gd_font_dir = <root>/assets/fonts) - GD server-side only, never served to the browser, so not a client loading concern.

Recommended priorities (highest leverage first): (1) kill the per-request full multilang.json decode - precompile a generated PHP array file (mtime-checked require) or load only _langs+current+default language; (2) raise media.php Cache-Control for immutable content-addressed qimg (max-age=3600 -> 604800+/immutable) since each revalidation re-bootstraps the app; (3) pre-render qimg files at attempt creation in take.php join so the first question view doesn't pay a synchronous GD render; (4) add .htaccess cache headers for assets/; (5) preconnect to cdn.jsdelivr.net in View head; (6) verify OPcache on host + app.debug=false in prod + composer dump-autoload -o --classmap-authoritative. Minor: Exam::saveAnswerFields re-fetches all answers per nav (targeted UPDATE would cut a SELECT); drawPartQuestions ORDER BY RAND() is join-time O(pool).

entities.name: MemoryStore
observations: SQLite-backed knowledge graph in src/Auth/MemoryStore.php
Own database file data/memory.sqlite, separate from auth database
Tables memory_entities / memory_relations
Every row scoped to a username for per-user isolation
create_relations only links existing entities; add_observations matches by name then id
Temporal model: added valid_from/valid_to columns (validity timeline) and updated_at on relations; migrated idempotently via PRAGMA table_info + ALTER TABLE in createSchema()

Mirrors entities into FTS5 virtual table memory_entities_fts (name, entity_type, observations) for zero-dependency BM25 keyword search; kept in sync on write and rebuilt once for pre-existing databases
searchGraph(): keyword = FTS5 BM25, semantic = IDF-weighted trigram similarity, hybrid = RRF fusion; hops>0 adds BFS expansion through relation hops
invalidateEntity() cascades to touching relations; invalidateRelation() closes validTo; re-creating an invalidated relation re-activates it

readGraph() now supports a scoped read: pass root (id or name, matched by name first) + depth (clamped 0-8) to get the subgraph within that many undirected relation hops; depth 0 returns just the root. Entities carry a distance field from the root; only relations with both endpoints in the subgraph are returned. Without root it reads the full graph as before; as_of and includeInvalid apply to scoped reads too.
BFS core extracted into private subgraphDistances(username, seeds, maxDepth, asOf, includeInvalid) — shared by search_graph's hops expansion (bfsExpand) and read_graph's scoped root/depth read

Access control (2026-08-02): all memory tools in MemoryTool.php now declare roles: ['user','admin'] — only logged-in accounts can list or call them; anonymous HTTP callers are hidden from tools/list and get -32001 on direct calls. Per-user isolation is unchanged (every row scoped by username). New self-onboarded accounts are granted the 'user' role; admin seed also carries 'user'.

readGraph() (2026-08-05) is lazy + paginated, three modes with precedence entity > subgraph > index: (1) entity — entityId set (matched by name first, then id) returns observations, timestamps, and every relation touching it; (2) subgraph — root + depth (0-8) returns full observations, entities carry distance, only relations whose both endpoints are inside are returned; (3) index (DEFAULT) — compact paginated entries id/name/entityType/relationCount plus validFrom/validTo, no observations, no relation list; limit clamped 1-1000 (default 100), offset default 0; response has mode/total/limit/offset/entities. Supersedes the old behavior where no-root read the full graph with all observations.

readGraph() subgraph mode (2026-08-05) is compact by default: entities carry id/name/entityType/distance/relationCount/validFrom/validTo and relations are topology-only (from/to/relationType), so a large-neighborhood orientation read stays small (~20KB for the 41-entity simplemcp subgraph vs ~60KB before). New include_observations flag (default false) opts into full detail: each entity's observations + created/updated timestamps and each relation's timestamps. Exposed via MemoryTool read_graph's include_observations arg.

2026-08-14: createEntities() gained a dedup guard — a new id whose name+entityType already exists under a different id is skipped and returned as a duplicate (return shape is now {ids, duplicates}); mergeEntities(keep, absorb) collapses duplicates atomically (merges observations deduped, re-points relations via copyRelations, deletes absorb).

2026-08-14: readSubgraph() reworked — relations filtered in SQL (from_entity IN ... AND to_entity IN ...), projection (entities/edges/both), direction (incoming/outgoing/both) via subgraphDistances, and limit/offset pagination with truncated/nextOffset continuation markers.

2026-08-14: searchGraph() gained includeRelations (attaches each hit's direct relations via relationsForIds()) and direction; new searchRelations() searches edges by exact relationType and/or endpoint with direction; new summary() returns node/edge counts + relation-type histogram + duplicate name+type groups + orphan count.

2026-08-14: createRelations() warns on relation types outside KNOWN_RELATION_TYPES; name-first matching now surfaces an ambiguity warning via ambiguityWarning()/nameMatches() when a name resolves to multiple entities.

2026-08-14 (supersedes the earlier 'dedup guard skips' note): duplicate detection is root-aware. projectRootsFor() resolves each entity's owning project-type entity by walking membership edges (MEMBERSHIP_TYPES: contains/core_component/entry_point/configured_by/part_of/belongs_to/implemented_in/decided/exposes). createEntities() no longer blocks on name+type — it always creates and returns informational duplicates (existing same-name+type ids with their roots) via potentialDuplicates(); summary() groups duplicates by (name, entityType, root projects) instead of name+type alone.

MEMBERSHIP_TYPES is deliberately narrower than KNOWN_RELATION_TYPES: 'uses'/'targets'/'adapted_from'/'requires' are excluded so a shared library (PHPMailer) has no root and two projects' composer.json files resolve to different roots.

2026-08-14: mergeEntities() gained a cross-root guard — when keep and an absorb entity have disjoint, non-empty root project sets it still merges but returns a warning (warnings[]), so a cross-project basename collision isn't silently collapsed. Roots are resolved up front via projectRootsFor() before the mutation transaction.

2026-09-11: MemoryStore::keywordSearch (src/Auth/MemoryStore.php:1477) had the identical inverted-FTS5-rank defect as DocumentStore — `ORDER BY rank DESC` on memory_entities_fts. Since FTS5's `rank` is a negated BM25 (smaller == better), DESC returned the WORST entities first, which silently degraded searchGraph keyword/hybrid result quality. Fixed in the same pass: DESC -> ASC with the same comment. Verified: `searchGraph('local', 'memory store FTS', 'keyword', 5, 0)` now ranks MemoryStore/DocumentStore/FTS5-related entities first.

2026-09-12: wholeRuns() committed — ftsMatchQuery() (src/Auth/MemoryStore.php:1690-1726) now also emits each underscored query run verbatim as a quoted prefix term via the new private wholeRuns() helper, mirroring DocumentStore exactly (same helper, same docblock rationale). Closes the identifier-tokenizer recall gap; the semantic (trigram) path remains the fuzzy/CJK fallback.

Wrapped batch operations in atomic database transactions for SQLite performance and ACID consistency.
Optimized createRelations endpoint checks using targeted WHERE id IN (...) queries.
Decoupled readIndex pagination into indexed entity selection and isolated relation count aggregation.
Added entity_type filtering across readGraph and searchGraph.

entities.name: OAuthServer
observations: Interactive OAuth 2.1 Authorization Code + PKCE in src/Auth/OAuthServer.php
Endpoints: /oauth/authorize, /oauth/token, /oauth/register
RFC 7591 dynamic client registration
Discovery: /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (RFC 8414) and /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (RFC 9728)
resolveUser() maps access token to UserContext
Advertises only none and client_secret_post (Cherry Studio fails with client_secret_basic)

GET/POST /oauth/authorize — validates the client and redirect URI (exact match, https-except-loopback), renders a two-step login (username, then password or onboarding), and on success redirects with a one-time code. Each login step also offers 'Continue anonymously' (anonymous=1): it skips login and issues a code bound to the reserved anonymous identity, which resolveUser() maps to UserContext::anonymous(). The reserved username is rejected by onboarding, so it can never collide with a real account.

POST /oauth/token — exchanges code + code_verifier for {access_token, refresh_token} and rotates refresh tokens. Confidential clients authenticate via client_secret_post (form body) or client_secret_basic (HTTP Basic) and may skip PKCE; public clients must use PKCE (S256). Only none and client_secret_post are advertised in discovery, so DCR-registered clients default to client_secret_post.

POST /oauth/register — RFC 7591 dynamic client registration: a client posts JSON (redirect_uris, token_endpoint_auth_method, ...) and receives a client_id plus a client_secret when confidential; registered clients persist in SQLite. The endpoint is advertised as registration_endpoint and can be protected with an initial access token (registration_access_token in config/oauth.php).

MCP JSON-RPC endpoint auth: a missing token maps to UserContext::anonymous() (only public tools listed/callable); a present-but-invalid/expired token is rejected with 401 + WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=...; a valid token is validated via findAccessToken (sha256-hashed at rest) and mapped to a UserContext. An OAuth token obtained via the authorize page's 'Continue anonymously' resolves to the same anonymous user.

For Open WebUI, use the pre-registered confidential client 'openwebui' and pick OAuth 2.1 (Static) when adding the MCP server, pasting the client id + secret; its redirect URI must be added to openwebui's redirect_uris.

entities.name: OTP verify/resend rate limiting is session-scoped only
observations: SECURITY REVIEW 2026-09-10 (attacker-reachability lens): VERIFIED exploitable, no refutation.

RateLimit (src/RateLimit.php) stores every counter under $_SESSION['rl'][$key]; keys used are 'otp_verify_'.email (verify.php:28,33,38) and 'otp_send_'.email (login.php:28,31). Dropping the simpleexam session cookie yields a new empty session = fresh 5-fail allowance, forever.

No server-side attempt counter exists: otp_codes columns (public_html/setup.php:40-52) are id,user_id,code_hash,purpose,expires_at,used_at,created_at - no attempts/failed_count. Otp::verify() (src/Otp.php verify()) just hash_equals the code_hash and returns; nothing is incremented on failure.
grep over the repo finds no REMOTE_ADDR / IP-keyed store anywhere.

Reachability confirmed: verify.php only redirects when App\Auth::user() is set (no auth gate); login.php is anonymous; Csrf::verify() (src/Csrf.php:27-33) is per-session and a fresh cookie jar gets a fresh valid token from GET, so CSRF is not an automation barrier. Bootstrap::run() has no global throttle/captcha (confirmed by grep).

Preconditions for the exploit: (a) know a registered email (login.php reveals 'no account' vs sent; app.registration_open=true in committed config.php lets the attacker register too) and (b) trigger a code via POST login.php for that email - both attacker-controllable.
verify.php performs no work delay; contrast take.php:680 sleep(1) on a wrong join code - the primitive exists but was not applied to OTP.

6-digit code from random_otp() (src/helpers.php:89-98, uniform random_int digit) = 10^6 space, TTL app.otp_ttl_minutes=10. Unlimited guesses per live code => full online account takeover of the only auth factor.
Severity HIGH confirmed. Recommended fix: atomic per-code attempts column (UPDATE ... WHERE attempts < N) + per-user/IP DB counter surviving cookie reset.

entities.name: Per-attempt secret as the student credential
observations: 2026-09-11: SimpleExam replaced name-based student identity with a per-attempt secret, closing SEC-04 (the only production-critical finding of the 2026-09-10 security audit).

THE FLAW: public_html/take.php bound the browser session to an attempt with 'SELECT id, status FROM attempts WHERE session_id = ? AND student_name = ?'. The join_code is deliberately shared with the whole class, so it is a room password, not a credential — any student could type a classmate's name and inherit that classmate's attempt, reading their saved answers live, overwriting them via Exam::saveAnswerFields, or submitting early to consume their remaining time. The attempts table collates utf8mb4_unicode_ci, so the match was also case- and accent-insensitive ('alice' matched 'Alice').

THE FIX (three parts): (1) attempts gained a CHAR(64) attempt_secret, generated as bin2hex(random_bytes(32)) at attempt creation and kept in $_SESSION['take']; (2) every later request resolves the attempt by 'WHERE id = ? AND attempt_secret = ?' — never by name; (3) joining with a name that already has an attempt is now REFUSED (new take.err_name_taken key in all 6 languages) instead of re-attaching. The join code is now used solely to create a first attempt.

The secret rule is applied uniformly to every consumer of $_SESSION['take']: take.php's resolution, media.php's ctx=qimg branch (query now joins attempts and requires t.attempt_secret), and media.php's ctx=a student branch (hash_equals against the row's secret). Holding an attempt id alone is no longer sufficient anywhere.

TRADE-OFF (deliberate, documented in README): an in-progress attempt resumes only in the browser that started it. Clearing cookies or switching device loses the attempt, and the student asks the teacher — the correct outcome, since the alternative is that anyone may re-enter anyone's paper. Existing rows were backfilled with secrets nobody holds, so an attempt mid-flight across the upgrade cannot be resumed.

Schema migration 22 adds the column and backfills, so no row is ever NULL in practice. Verified on the dev DB 2026-09-11: migration applied, 15/15 attempts got distinct 64-char secrets; the hijack simulation (name lookup finds the victim row) is now refused, resolution with a wrong or absent secret is denied, and a fresh name still creates an attempt (8 answers drawn) whose exam page resolves correctly through the secret.

observations: src/QuestionImage.php — App\QuestionImage, GD-based question-text-to-PNG renderer (anti-scraping)

available()/enabled() gate: extension_loaded('gd') && imagettftext && fonts present && config app.question_image_enabled; falls back silently to plain escaped text when GD/fonts missing so exams always work

canRender($text) needs a font covering the text; CJK regex /[\x{4E00}-\x{9FFF}\x{3400}-\x{4DBF}\x{F900}-\x{FAFF}\x{AC00}-\x{D7AF}]/u picks the bundled CJK font (wqy-microhei.ttc face 0) vs DejaVu Sans for Latin
hashFor($kind,$answer) = sha256(normalize(text)|RENDER_VERSION|kind|font|width|size|colors|pad); also the question_images cache key; normalize() strips CR so URL hash and rendered bytes always agree

renderFor($kind,$answer): manual wrap via imagettfbbox (imagettftext never wraps), CJK char tokenizer, explicit \n hard break, ~40 line cap then truncate with '…'; canvas allocated AFTER wrapping; solid white bg, dark text, no alpha; returns PNG bytes
Constants: STATEMENT_WIDTH=720 / OPTION_WIDTH=680, PAD=16, LINE_HEIGHT=1.5, MAX_LINES=40, RENDER_VERSION='v1' — bump RENDER_VERSION if fonts/layout change to invalidate the image cache
GD gotchas handled: TrueType only (CFF/OTF breaks some FreeType builds), never HTML-escapes before imagettftext (wants raw UTF-8), never touches the questions table or correct_index

2026-09-02 (raw formatting fix): wrap() now preserves raw spacing — whitespace-run tokens are appended verbatim instead of being collapsed into a single separator, so consecutive spaces and per-line leading indentation render exactly as typed in the teacher's textarea. Only whitespace at a wrap boundary is dropped: emitted lines are rtrim'd, and a wrapped continuation line never inherits a mid-line space (indent stays a paragraph-start property). Hard \n linebreaks were already preserved (each paragraph becomes its own line; empty paragraph = blank line). Verified on dev PHP 8.4.22 + bundled DejaVu fonts: 'following   statements' keeps its 3 spaces, '    (i)  ...' keeps its 4-space indent and double spaces; CJK mixed text keeps raw spaces too. Note: GD renders a literal \t as a ~14px gap (not tofu, not zero-width), so pasted tabs are safe. Renderer pre-render caching (content-addressed hashFor) is unaffected because normalize() only normalizes CR/LF, not internal whitespace.

Rendering/API note for back-compat: the statement text still passes through the global post() helper (helpers.php) in question_form.php on save, which trims leading/trailing whitespace of the WHOLE statement string only — end-of-line indentation and internal spacing are unaffected; a blank line at the very start/end of the statement is still stripped before storage.

entities.name: Rate limits stored server-side, not in the session
observations: 2026-09-11: SimpleExam moved every rate-limit counter out of $_SESSION into a `rate_limits` table, closing SEC-07 of the 2026-09-10 audit. All counters previously lived in $_SESSION['rl'], so discarding the cookie reset the OTP lockout, the OTP resend throttle and the join-code lockout — a six-digit code with a lockout the attacker can clear at will is a six-digit code with no lockout.

SCHEMA: migration 24 creates `rate_limits (bucket VARCHAR(32), rl_key VARCHAR(191), fails SMALLINT UNSIGNED, window_at DATETIME, locked_until DATETIME NULL, PRIMARY KEY (bucket, rl_key), KEY idx_rate_limits_window (window_at))`. Added to setup.php's DDL for fresh installs.

API: App\RateLimit keeps the same primitives but takes an explicit bucket — tooSoon/mark(bucket, key, seconds), fail(bucket, key, max, lockSeconds), locked/lockRemaining/reset(bucket, key). Buckets in use: 'otp_send' (keyed by email), 'otp_verify' (email), 'join' (session_id:name), 'join_ip' (session_id:client-IP). Keys are lower-cased and hashed with sha256 when longer than the column, so an over-long key can never collide.

CONCURRENCY: fail() reads the row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside a transaction (joining a caller's if one is open, matching Credits::adjust's contract) so two racing requests cannot both read '4 failures' and each write '5'. A key that is already locked is returned as still-locked without extending the lock. A DB error is logged and treated as 'not limited' — failing closed would lock every user out of login the moment this one table is unavailable, and the same database holds users/otp_codes so login is already broken in that case.
GC: finished counters older than 24h are swept opportunistically (1-in-50 chance per mark()), so the table stays bounded without a cron.

DESIGN TRADE-OFF — the join code carries TWO counters. The per-name one ('join', 5 fails) is the friendly lockout a student sees. It cannot bound a brute force alone because the name is free text — an attacker just types a different one — so a second counter ('join_ip', default 100 fails via app.join_max_fails_per_ip) applies per session + client IP across names. The IP threshold is deliberately generous: locking a whole class out of an exam mid-sitting is far worse than a marginal increase in guessing ease, and the real fix for guessable codes is a longer minimum code (SEC-18, still open).

CLIENT IP BEHIND CLOUDFLARE: the new helpers.php client_ip() prefers HTTP_CF_CONNECTING_IP and falls back to REMOTE_ADDR. That header is trustworthy ONLY because the origin is not directly reachable — the site is served exclusively through Cloudflare (which also forces HTTPS). If the origin ever becomes directly reachable, a client could spoof the header and rotate past an IP-scoped limit.

REMOVED sleep(1): the join flow used to sleep 1s per wrong code, which was the only single-threaded brake and a DoS vector (each wrong guess pinned a PHP worker for a second). With real counters it was redundant. Attempt volume is now bounded by the IP counter, and once locked further attempts cost only one SELECT.

attempt(): called from Auth::boot() when no session user exists; validates cookie token against DB, checks expiry + user active, then ROTATES the token (deletes old row, inserts fresh one, rewrites cookie) so a stolen/replayed cookie is already dead on next use

entities.name: Remembered sessions expire, and the token is revoked with them
observations: 2026-09-11: SimpleExam made session expiry apply to 'remember me' sessions and tied refresh-token revocation to it, closing SEC-13 of the 2026-09-10 audit. A session marked $_SESSION['remember'] was exempt from the idle timeout (comment: 'their durability comes from the revocable refresh token') and there was no absolute lifetime at all, so a stolen cookie stayed usable for the token's full 30 days.

FIX: Bootstrap::run() now applies the idle timeout (app.idle_timeout_minutes, default 120) to EVERY session plus an absolute cap (app.session_max_hours, default 12) measured from $_SESSION['auth_time'], which Auth::login() and Auth::restoreFromRememberToken() both set. Auth gained public forgetRememberToken() (wrapper over the existing clearRememberToken()).

THE LOAD-BEARING DETAIL: the refresh token is revoked when the session expires. Without that the whole control is theatre — the next request finds no session, restoreFromRememberToken() rebuilds one from the still-valid token (it runs earlier in Bootstrap, gated only on empty($_SESSION['user_id'])), and the timeout accomplishes nothing. This is the difference between a control that exists in code and one that exists in practice.

DELIBERATE TRADE-OFF: an idle timeout now costs a remembered user a fresh OTP. That is what an idle timeout means, and both windows are configurable. A session RESTORED from a token gets its own fresh clock (auth_time = now), so the absolute cap measures continuous session age rather than age since the token was first issued — which keeps 'remember me for 30 days' working across browser restarts.

KNOWN RESIDUAL (recorded, not fixed): the remember-me token is still a non-rotating bearer credential — it is not reissued on use and has no per-user revocation beyond the single-device clear. Token rotation on each use is the durable mitigation for a *stolen* token (the thief and the legitimate user would then conflict, surfacing the theft), and was deliberately left out of scope.

VERIFIED both directions on the dev DB 2026-09-11: an active remembered session idle ~27h is wiped AND its auth_tokens row deleted, with a follow-up request staying logged out; conversely a fresh (empty) session carrying a valid token still restores normally (user_id set, remember true, auth_time set, token retained), so remember-me is intact.

entities.name: Revocable remember-me refresh token
observations: 2026-08-25: remember-me is implemented as a DB-backed revocable refresh token, NOT a long-lived session cookie. The user explicitly rejected the session-cookie-extension approach ('use refresh token so it revokeable'). Raw token lives only in the simpleexam_remember cookie; the DB stores sha256 only, so a DB leak exposes no usable tokens. Fixed 30-day expiry from issue (not sliding) so a stolen token can't extend itself. No rotation on use (avoids multi-tab races); revocation at logout + on any plain login is the security bound. Logout revokes only the current device's token; the (user_id, expires_at) index leaves room for a future log-out-everywhere admin action. Remembered sessions skip the idle-timeout wipe since durability comes from the token, and no session.gc_maxlifetime change is needed — a GC'd session is simply re-created by auto-login.

2026-09-11 (SEC-13 fix, working tree on branch security/attempt-credential-and-bonus-gate, NOT yet committed): the remember-me idle-timeout exemption is GONE. Bootstrap now applies BOTH windows to every session, remembered ones included — idle = app.idle_timeout_minutes (120 min) and a NEW absolute cap app.session_max_hours (12h since $_SESSION['auth_time'], stamped by Auth::login and by each restore). On expiry it calls Auth::forgetRememberToken() before clearing $_SESSION; without that revoke the next request would restore from the still-valid 30-day token and the timeout would mean nothing.

Still true: raw token only in the simpleexam_remember cookie, sha256 only in auth_tokens, fixed 30-day expiry from issue, no rotation on use, logout revokes only this device, plain (non-remember) login revokes any lingering token. Auth::restoreFromRememberToken() still runs before the expiry check and gives a restored session a fresh clock, so a restore is never immediately wiped.

2026-08-20 (supersedes the 'idempotent migrations run on every boot' description): Schema::patch() is now a VERSIONED migration runner. Schema::VERSION = 17, DB tracks progress in a schema_versions table (version INT PK, applied_at DATETIME). Fast path: SELECT MAX(version) FROM schema_versions == VERSION -> return immediately (one indexed read, NO information_schema guards or DDL/DML on the happy path). The ~10 guards + ~13 DDL/DML statements the old unversioned patch() fired per request are gone.

migrations() returns version => [reason, needs closure, sql string|array] for 1..17: 1 attempt_minutes, 2 deadline_at, 3-4 questions image/audio_path, 5-6 answers image/audio_path, 7 DROP question_images, 8 deadline-reconcile UPDATE, 9 CREATE exam_parts, 10 CREATE exam_session_parts, 11 questions.part_id+KEY+FK, 12 backfill 'Part 1', 13 backfill questions.part_id, 14 backfill exam_session_parts, 15-16 widen type ENUMs to handwriting, 17 answers.drawing_json. Order preserves the old patch() sequence; 'needs' guards keep every migration idempotent (safe re-run after a mid-migration failure).

Slow path (dbVersion < VERSION): create schema_versions if missing, run each unapplied migration whose 'needs' is true, log 'Schema: applied migration N (reason): <sql>' to error_log (the 'give me the query' behavior), then INSERT the version. A failed SQL is logged and NOT recorded -> retried next boot. A legacy install with the current schema records all 17 as no-ops in one pass.

dbVersion() treats a missing schema_versions table as version 0 (creates it on catch) so a DB reset/legacy install triggers the full migration pass; a DB version AHEAD of code (rolled-back deploy) logs a warning and does nothing. Static $done flag makes patch() run once per process.
hasColumn() is now public (cron scripts assert attempts.deadline_at); hasTable/countMatches/typeNeedsHandwriting/exec are private helpers.

entities.name: Seed re-insertion caused duplicate variant groups
observations: Found + fixed 2026-08-08. Symptom: saving any variant product (esp. Kaos Polos, id 16, combination mode) duplicated every variant group after save, and POS then showed 'Variant not found' when selecting the product

Root cause: Database::getInstance() runs Database::seed() in the constructor, and PHP built-in server spawns a NEW process per request, so seed.sql runs on EVERY request. seed.sql seeds Kaos Polos variant data with EXPLICIT ids (groups 1-2, options 1-5, variants 1-6, links). Product::update() deletes + recreates a product's variant rows with NEW auto-increment ids on save; the next request's seed then finds the old explicit ids free and re-inserts them -> product ends up with BOTH the saved set and the re-seeded set

Fix in database/seed.sql: latch the bootstrap decision once into session var @seed_kaos_polos = (product 16 has has_variants=1) AND (product 16 has no variant_groups), then every variant-data insert becomes INSERT..SELECT..FROM DUAL WHERE @seed_kaos_polos. Per-statement NOT EXISTS guards would break (the first group insert flips the guard false for the rest); the latched var makes the whole block run (fresh install) or skip (product already has groups)

Impact: seed only re-seeds variant data for a fresh install; any saved/edited product keeps its own variant rows. Existing dup data was cleaned by deleting all of product 16's variant rows then letting the guarded seed re-create the original set

Verification: real UI save of Kaos Polos -> 2 groups / 6 variants / 12 links, no duplicates after subsequent request runs seed; POS variant selection + add-to-cart works; dimension product (Teh Manis) MIN semantics unchanged

entities.name: Signup bonus paid on first email verification
observations: 2026-09-11: SimpleExam moved the 5-credit signup bonus from registration to the first successful OTP verification, closing SEC-06 (a live, unlimited credit-farming path — registration_open is true in production).

THE FLAW: public_html/register.php inserted the user, called Credits::signupBonus() immediately, and only THEN called Otp::issue(). There was no email_verified_at column anywhere in the schema, so a never-verified account was fully functional and already credited — anyone could mint unlimited teacher accounts at 5 free exam sessions each, the only cost being a throwaway mailbox.

THE FIX: users gained email_verified_at DATETIME NULL (migration 23). register.php now creates the account with nothing credited. verify.php calls the new Credits::onFirstVerification() after a successful code check, which pays the bonus exactly once, guarded by 'UPDATE users SET email_verified_at = NOW() WHERE id = ? AND email_verified_at IS NULL' — only the caller that flips the row out of NULL sees rowCount 1, so replays, races and second-device logins grant nothing. The stamp and the grant share one transaction: if the grant fails, the stamp rolls back so the next login retries them together rather than leaving an account verified but unpaid.

ADMIN-CREATED ACCOUNTS KEEP THE OLD BEHAVIOUR: users.php (admin creates a teacher) and setup.php (seeds the admin) insert with email_verified_at = NOW() — the admin vouches for the address — and credit immediately. Because the column is already set, onFirstVerification is a no-op for them, so the bonus is never paid twice.

MIGRATION 23 grandfathers every account that already has a signup_bonus ledger row (email_verified_at := created_at), so the migration-19 backfill and any earlier registration are not paid a second time on their next login. Accounts with no bonus row stay NULL and are paid when they first verify.

Verified on the dev DB 2026-09-11: a freshly registered account has 0 credits and NULL verification; after one onFirstVerification it has 5 credits and one ledger row; two further calls change nothing; an admin-style insert (verified at INSERT) plus signupBonus plus onFirstVerification yields exactly 5. The dev DB's pre-existing user was correctly grandfathered (email_verified_at = created_at, credits unchanged at 116).
