CORRECTION (2026-09-10 security audit, verified): earlier KG observations claiming config.php, src/, vendor/ and storage/ 'sit above the docroot / are not web-accessible' are based on a deployment layout the README contradicts. README.md:273-289 instructs FTPing the whole project root into InfinityFree's htdocs/ so that htdocs/public_html/, htdocs/src/, htdocs/config.php coexist - which makes the PROJECT ROOT the docroot, not its parent. Under that documented layout every non-public_html path (config.php, multilang.json, storage/, cli/, composer.lock, .git/) is INSIDE the served tree and protected only by the root .htaccess rewrite into public_html/ plus its FilesMatch denies. The direct risk is contained (PHP files execute rather than download, and FilesMatch denies config.php/logs/composer), but storage/media/ has NO explicit deny rule and would be served verbatim if mod_rewrite ever failed or AllowOverride disallowed rewrite. SEC-22 in the 2026-09-10 audit. Fix: pick one model and make docs match, and add explicit 'Require all denied' to storage/ and cli/ rather than depending on the catch-all rewrite.

CORRECTION (2026-09-10 security audit, verified): several KG observations describe config.php as 'gitignored' or as living outside version control. That is FALSE. config.php is tracked (git ls-files config.php succeeds), was added by commit 26ade7f 'Track config', and .gitignore covers only .env*, /vendor/ and /storage/. The file is in HEAD and in every clone of the public repo github.com/FishyBoat21/SimpleExam, together with its DOKU client_id + sandbox secret_key, a Brevo/SMTP application password, the production admin_email, and the defaults debug=true, installed=false, registration_open=true.

entities.name: SimpleExam security audit (2026-09-10)
observations: 2026-09-10: full multi-agent security audit of SimpleExam over 10 attack-surface dimensions (secrets/config, auth+session, authz/IDOR, student exam flow, payments/credits, uploads/media, injection+XSS, infra/deploy, data integrity, business-logic abuse). 228 agents; every candidate finding adversarially verified by 3 diverse lenses (attacker reachability, code accuracy, impact calibration); a completeness critic ran a final pass. Result: 27 unique verified findings - 6 critical, 9 high, 13 medium, 12 low; 17 candidates rejected (including several duplicates of confirmed findings, which is why the raw 'refuted' count is higher than the number of genuinely distinct false positives).

Data-hygiene caveat: 3 candidates (Brevo SMTP key exposure, DOKU secret exposure, signup-bonus farming) were recorded as 'refuted' ONLY because all three of their verifiers crashed at the model provider with a content-filter error - the prompts embedded the literal secret values. They are NOT genuine refutations; each duplicates a finding confirmed by a separate agent and independently re-verified by direct code inspection during the audit.

Deliverable: a standalone HTML assessment report at d:/Project/simpleexam-security-audit.html - deliberately OUTSIDE the git repo, with the credential values redacted in the text. Artifact publishing was unavailable in this session (it authenticates with ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN rather than a claude.ai login).

CRITICAL SEC-01 (auth bypass): the OTP login flow prints the plaintext 6-digit code on screen for ANY account. src/Mailer.php:17-19 returns false (not throws) when smtp.host is empty; src/Otp.php:53-60 treats that false as 'demo mode' and flashes the plaintext code; src/View.php:107-120 echoes flash messages UNESCAPED by design (the demo string carries markup). config.php:106 ships smtp.host=''. Unauthenticated admin takeover in two requests: GET login.php for a CSRF token, POST the admin email, read the code off verify.php, POST it. Reached independently by two finders, 3/3 votes each.

CRITICAL SEC-02 (free credits): the committed DOKU secret_key lets an anonymous attacker forge the payment webhook. src/Doku.php:239-263 (verifyNotification) is the sole gate on the public public_html/doku_notify.php; it validates only the HMAC, never Client-Id, the notified amount, a timestamp window, or a replay cache. Invoice numbers are 'SE-' . an auto-increment (public_html/credits.php:53), enumerable. Full chain: clone repo -> read secret -> register -> create a pending order -> POST a hand-signed SUCCESS -> Credits::grantOrder credits the order. Chain, not a single bug.

CRITICAL SEC-03 (secret exposure): config.php is TRACKED in git (not covered by .gitignore, which lists .env*, /vendor/, /storage/) and was added by commit 26ade7f 'Track config'. It carries the DOKU client_id + sandbox secret_key, a Brevo/SMTP application password, the production admin_email, and the insecure defaults debug=true / installed=false / registration_open=true. Any KG observation claiming config.php is gitignored is STALE and wrong. Rotation is insufficient without purging the file from git history.

CRITICAL SEC-04 (exam integrity): student identity is a free-text name, not a credential. public_html/take.php:691 binds the browser session to an attempt via 'SELECT id, status FROM attempts WHERE session_id = ? AND student_name = ?'. Because the join_code is deliberately shared with the whole class, any student who types a classmate's name inherits that attempt id and can read (renderExam shows saved radio/essay/drawing), overwrite (Exam::saveAnswerFields updates WHERE attempt_id = the hijacker's), or force-submit the victim's attempt. The attempts table collates utf8mb4_unicode_ci, so the name match is case- and accent-insensitive. Fix: issue a per-attempt attempt_secret and resolve by id+secret.

CRITICAL SEC-05 (unauthenticated installer): public_html/setup.php's only lock is the app.installed config flag, and NO code path anywhere writes that flag - the operator must hand-edit config.php. The committed config ships it false, so /setup.php is permanently reachable: any anonymous GET runs the full DDL sequence, promotes/creates the admin account for app.admin_email, and prints that email back to the caller. It also echoes raw PDO exception text ($e->getMessage()) while app.debug=true. Revisiting after an admin deletion recreates the admin.

CRITICAL SEC-06 (credit farming): public_html/register.php:62-67 inserts the user, calls Credits::signupBonus() FIRST, and only then issues the OTP - so the 5-credit bonus is paid before the email is ever verified. There is no email_verified / verified_at column anywhere in the schema, so a never-verified account is fully functional. Combined with registration_open=true (config.php:54) and session-scoped rate limiting, anyone can mint unlimited teacher accounts at 5 free exam sessions each.

HIGH: (a) SEC-07 all rate limiting is session-scoped - src/RateLimit.php stores every counter in $_SESSION['rl'], so discarding the cookie resets the OTP lockout, the resend throttle, and the join-code lockout; (b) SEC-08 the exam deadline is bypassed by a CLIENT-SUPPLIED timeout=1 flag - public_html/take.php:51-57 exempts it from the only server-side deadline check and the submit branch at 572-590 never re-checks; (c) SEC-09 no HTTPS enforcement (the redirect in public_html/.htaccess:14 is commented out), no HSTS, and the Secure cookie flag is derived from $_SERVER['HTTPS'] rather than set unconditionally; (d) SEC-10 public_html/session_delete.php:26-42 refunds without checking $del->rowCount(), so two concurrent deletes double-refund (a credit mint); (e) SEC-11 app.debug=true ships on, so display_errors=E_ALL leaks SQLSTATE text, absolute paths and stack traces; (f) SEC-12 src/CreditOrderReconciler.php:131 closes a still-pending order to failed once the DOKU window passes, so a late-settling QRIS payment is taken without granting credits; (g) SEC-13 a 'remember me' session is permanently exempt from the idle timeout with no absolute cap; (h) SEC-14 login.php and register.php are account-existence oracles with no rate limit; (i) SEC-15 the question-text-as-PNG anti-cheating control is cosmetic.

NOTABLE FALSE POSITIVES (correctly rejected, and evidence the codebase is sound where it was carefully built): SQL injection was looked for across every query and NOT found - the prepared-statement discipline is complete, including the two places that interpolate a column name (questions.php:88's sort_order uses (int) cast; question_delete.php and media.php interpolate a $col drawn from a fixed set). The upload path's extension allowlist, MIME validation and basename() traversal forcing all held. media.php's Range parser, response headers, and its qimg authorization branch (attempt-scoped + recomputed content hash) were verified sound. Credits::adjust's atomic conditional UPDATE and grantOrder's status='pending' guard genuinely prevent double-spend and double-grant. Every teacher route is ownership-scoped in SQL via JOIN exams e ... WHERE e.user_id = ?. Both cli/ scripts are correctly guarded by PHP_SAPI !== 'cli'.

PRODUCTION CONTEXT CORRECTION (user, 2026-09-10) — supersedes the severity framing recorded earlier for this audit: (1) the repository github.com/FishyBoat21/SimpleExam is PRIVATE, not public; (2) production SETS smtp.host; (3) production sets app.debug = false. The committed config.php is therefore the DEVELOPMENT config, not the production one. The report was revised to Rev 2 and re-scored rather than having the findings removed.

REVISED SEVERITIES (Rev 2): the two-request unauthenticated admin takeover is NOT reachable in production — with smtp.host set, Mailer::sendLoginOtp never returns false, so the plaintext code is never flashed, and a delivery FAILURE correctly throws into the otp.flash_failed branch. SEC-01 is RETAINED at High as a fail-open code defect: the safe behaviour requires a setting to be present, its absence produces no error and no log, and it is reachable again from a staging environment, a redeploy from the repo before the config is filled in, or a lost SMTP setting. SEC-02 (forged DOKU webhook via the committed secret) and SEC-03 (credentials in version control) drop to Medium — private repo, and the committed DOKU values are SANDBOX credentials, so production credits are at risk only if production shares that secret. debug=true disclosure drops to Medium/Low (production overrides it; the repository ships the unsafe default).

REVISED TOP FINDING IS SEC-04, the only production-critical item and unaffected by every configuration correction: the student exam flow has no credential for the student. public_html/take.php:691 binds the session to an attempt via 'SELECT id, status FROM attempts WHERE session_id = ? AND student_name = ?'; the join code is shared with the whole class by design, so any student who types a classmate's name inherits that attempt and can read, overwrite, or force-submit it. The attempts table collates utf8mb4_unicode_ci so the match is case- and accent-insensitive. Fix: per-attempt attempt_secret stored on the row, resolved by id+secret on every request, join code used only for first-attempt creation.

STILL LIVE IN PRODUCTION (all configuration-independent code defects): SEC-04 (above); SEC-08 the exam deadline is bypassed by a client-supplied timeout=1 flag (take.php:51-57 exempts it from the only server-side deadline check and the submit branch at 572-590 never re-checks); SEC-07 all rate limiting is session-scoped ($_SESSION['rl'], src/RateLimit.php); SEC-09 no HTTPS enforcement and both cookies derive Secure from $_SERVER['HTTPS']; SEC-10 session_delete.php double-refunds on a concurrent delete (no $del->rowCount() check); SEC-12 CreditOrderReconciler closes a pending order once expired_at passes, forfeiting a late QRIS settlement; SEC-13 remembered sessions are exempt from the idle timeout with no absolute cap; SEC-17 unlimited attempts/retakes via ?action=new.

THREE OPEN QUESTIONS asked but not yet answered — each moves a finding by more than one severity band: (a) is production app.installed true (or is setup.php deleted)? If yes SEC-05 drops to Low; if no it is a live unauthenticated installer that creates the admin account on demand and returns to CRITICAL. (b) is production registration_open false? If yes SEC-06 drops to Medium; if no it stays High (anyone can create credited accounts). (c) does production use a DIFFERENT DOKU secret than the committed sandbox one? If different, SEC-02/SEC-03 drop to Low; if the same, both return to CRITICAL immediately and the secret must be rotated today.

OPEN QUESTIONS RESOLVED (user, 2026-09-10) — report finalized as Rev 3. (a) app.installed IS true in production (setup.php is still present on the server but now exits early into its 'already installed' page) → SEC-05 DOWNGRADED from Critical to Low; it stays in the report only as the code defect that the lock is a hand-edited boolean no code path ever writes, and would return to Critical the moment someone resets installed for a re-install over an existing DB. (b) registration_open is STILL TRUE in production → SEC-06 CONFIRMED LIVE AND UNLIMITED at High; this is now one of the two most urgent items alongside SEC-04. (c) production uses SEPARATE DOKU credentials from the committed sandbox values → SEC-02 DOWNGRADED from Critical to Low for the money path (the committed sandbox secret cannot grant production credits); its missing Client-Id/amount/timestamp/replay validation is retained as defence in depth.

FINAL Rev 3 SEVERITY COUNTS (27 unique findings): 1 Critical, 8 High, 11 Medium, 7 Low, 17 rejected. THE TWO LIVE ITEMS: SEC-04 (student identity is a typed name — the only Critical) and SEC-06 (signup bonus paid before email verification with registration open — High). Remaining live Highs: SEC-08 deadline bypass via client-supplied timeout=1; SEC-07 session-scoped rate limiting; SEC-09 no HTTPS enforcement; SEC-10 concurrent session-delete double refund; SEC-12 reconciler forfeits a late-settling QRIS payment; SEC-13 remembered sessions exempt from the idle timeout. Latent High: SEC-01 fail-open demo OTP. Mediums: SEC-03 (committed credentials — see below), SEC-11 debug=true default, SEC-14 enumeration oracle, SEC-15 cosmetic PNG anti-cheat, SEC-16 register race, SEC-17 unlimited attempts, SEC-18 short join codes, SEC-19 metadata oracle, SEC-20 unthrottled order creation, SEC-21 unbounded uploads/no render GC, SEC-27 week-long media cache. Lows: SEC-02, SEC-05, SEC-22 deployment-rewrite dependency, SEC-23 media.php uncaught exception, SEC-24 missing headers, SEC-25 raw flash XSS channel, SEC-26 sequential ids.

ONE RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY (only affects SEC-03): is the Brevo SMTP key committed in config.php the SAME credential production uses to send OTP mail? The DOKU values in that file are confirmed sandbox-only, but production sets smtp.host in the same file that carries the Brevo key, which suggests the mail key IS production's — in which case anyone with repo access can send SPF/DKIM-authentic mail as noreply@jch.my.id. If production has a separate mail credential, SEC-03 drops to Low as well. Rotating the key closes the question either way.

FIX LANDED 2026-09-11 — SEC-04 (student attempt hijack) closed. public_html/take.php no longer resolves an attempt by typed name: the session's attempt is looked up by 'WHERE id = ? AND attempt_secret = ?', and joining with a name that already has an attempt is refused (new take.err_name_taken key, all 6 languages). New migration 22 adds attempts.attempt_secret CHAR(64) and backfills every existing row. media.php's ctx=qimg and ctx=a student branches now both require the secret too. See [[se-decision-attempt-credential]]. Verified end-to-end over HTTP on the dev DB.

FIX LANDED 2026-09-11 — SEC-06 (signup-bonus farming before verification) closed. register.php no longer credits at INSERT; verify.php calls the new Credits::onFirstVerification(), which stamps users.email_verified_at and pays the bonus exactly once (guarded by the conditional UPDATE's rowCount, both in one transaction). Admin-created accounts (users.php) and the seeded admin (setup.php) are stamped verified at INSERT and keep the immediate bonus. New migration 23 adds the column and grandfathers every account that already had a signup_bonus ledger row. See [[se-decision-bonus-on-verification]].

FIX LANDED 2026-09-11 — SEC-02 (forgeable payment webhook) closed by REMOVAL. The user confirmed doku_notify.php was deprecated, so the endpoint was deleted (git rm) along with Doku::verifyNotification() and its private header() helper. Payment confirmation is now pull-only: the customer's back-to-merchant redirect runs an active Check Status query in payment_return.php, and App\CreditOrderReconciler re-checks timed-out orders on the cron, so an order still settles when the customer never returns. Credits::grantOrder remains the single idempotent grant path (status='pending' guard). README and the Doku/CreditOrderReconciler/payment_return docblocks were updated.

ADJACENT BUG FIXED WHILE ADDING THE MIGRATIONS: public_html/setup.php's schema-version seeding guard tested answers.drawing_json, the newest column as of ~VERSION 17. An older DB being re-installed over (app.installed reset) that already had drawing_json would have been stamped with the CURRENT Schema::VERSION, skipping every later migration — including 22 and 23, leaving the new columns missing. The guard now tests users.email_verified_at (the newest column) with a comment that it must be bumped whenever a migration adds a column. Note this path is unreachable in production while app.installed=true, but reachable on any dev/re-install with installed=false.

VERIFICATION EVIDENCE (2026-09-11, dev DB): all PHP files lint clean; multilang.json parses with exact 485-key parity across all 6 languages; migrations 22+23 applied cleanly and are logged by Schema::patch; the dev DB's single pre-existing user was grandfathered rather than double-paid; all 15 existing attempts received distinct 64-char secrets. Live HTTP test with the session window temporarily opened: the old name-based hijack lookup still finds the victim row but is now REFUSED, while a fresh name creates an attempt (8 answers drawn) and take.php follows the redirect into the exam page resolved via the secret. All probe rows deleted and the window restored exactly; the dev DB is back to 1 user / 15 attempts.

FIX LANDED 2026-09-11 (working tree, uncommitted on branch security/attempt-credential-and-bonus-gate) — SEC-13 (remembered sessions exempt from the idle timeout with no absolute cap) closed. src/Bootstrap.php now applies BOTH windows to every session including remembered ones: idle = app.idle_timeout_minutes (120 min) and a new absolute cap app.session_max_hours (12h since $_SESSION['auth_time']). On expiry it calls the new Auth::forgetRememberToken() (Bootstrap->Auth public wrapper over clearRememberToken) before emptying $_SESSION, so the still-valid 30-day cookie cannot silently re-authenticate. Auth::login and Auth::restoreFromRememberToken each stamp a fresh auth_time. Deliberate trade-off recorded in the code comments: an idle timeout now costs a remembered user a fresh OTP.

CLOSURE STATUS 2026-09-11 (report Rev 4): all nine production-affecting findings from Rev 3 are closed — SIX FIXED IN CODE: SEC-04 (per-attempt secret), SEC-06 (bonus on first verification), SEC-07 (server-side rate limits), SEC-08 (deadline enforced on submit), SEC-10 (refund guard), SEC-13 (session expiry + token revocation); TWO CLOSED BY DEPLOYMENT/DESIGN: SEC-09 and SEC-12; ONE REMOVED: SEC-02 (doku_notify.php deleted). Remaining: 0 Critical, 1 High (SEC-01), 11 Medium, 5 Low, plus one new Medium (SEC-28). Two commits on branch security/attempt-credential-and-bonus-gate: 411a8eb (SEC-04/06/02) and c13b7da (SEC-07/08/10/13).

SEC-08 FIX: the exam deadline was enforced in exactly one place — the lazy auto-finalize at the top of take.php — and that check was explicitly skipped for a request carrying timeout=1. The submit branch below never re-checked, so a student could keep answering past the deadline and submit whenever they chose. The deadline is now enforced INSIDE the submit branch: lateBy = time() - strtotime(Exam::attemptDeadline(...)) is compared against app.submit_grace_seconds (default 0) plus a new top-level constant SUBMIT_LATE_TOLERANCE_SECONDS = 15. The tolerance exists because the timer runs in the student's browser and the request lands a second or two late through no fault of theirs; 15s absorbs that without buying working time. When late, saveAnswerFields is skipped (with an error_log trace) and the attempt finalizes against what was already stored. VERIFIED: with the window closed two hours earlier, a timeout=1 POST carrying an answer finalized the attempt but the answer was NOT persisted (chosen_index stayed NULL).

SEC-10 FIX: both public_html/session_delete.php and public_html/exam_delete.php refunded a credit WITHOUT checking that their DELETE had affected a row, across three non-transactional queries — so two concurrent deletes of the same session/exam both observed 'charged, no attempts' and both refunded, minting a credit. Both paths now: (a) open a transaction, (b) lock the parent row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE first so a concurrent delete blocks rather than races past, (c) read the attempt count and the session_create ledger row INSIDE the transaction, and (d) refund only when $del->rowCount() === 1. A failed refund throws so the whole delete rolls back rather than silently losing the credit. NOTE: exam_delete.php had the identical defect and was fixed in the same pass. VERIFIED with two independent DB connections: the second blocked 2.0s on the first's lock, then its delete matched zero rows and refunded nothing — exactly one refund row, net credits zero. Exercised at the DB layer because PHP's built-in server is single-threaded on Windows so a true two-request race cannot be reproduced over HTTP; the serialization is InnoDB row locking.

CORRECTION 2026-09-11 (maintainer): SEC-12 was WRONG and is closed, not fixed. It claimed CreditOrderReconciler could close a pending order moments before a late QRIS settlement arrived, taking the money without granting credits. That cannot happen: the DOKU checkout's payment_due_date is set from the same app.credit_payment_timeout_minutes value the reconciler uses, so by the time an order is eligible to be closed its QRIS has genuinely expired and the customer can no longer pay it. The two clocks are the same clock. Anyone re-reading the Rev 3 text should treat SEC-12 as withdrawn.

CORRECTION 2026-09-11 (maintainer): SEC-09 is CLOSED BY DEPLOYMENT, not fixed in code. The site is served exclusively through Cloudflare, which forces HTTPS, so the plaintext-HTTP path the finding described is unreachable. Two code-level remnants were noted but deliberately not acted on: the session/remember cookie 'secure' flag is still derived from $_SERVER['HTTPS'] (which the origin may not see behind a TLS-terminating proxy), and the remember-me token is still a non-rotating bearer credential. Both are harmless while Cloudflare stays in front of the origin, and the second becomes relevant again if the token is exposed by any other route.

NEW FINDING SEC-28 (Medium, introduced by the SEC-04 fix — record it honestly): because public_html/take.php now REFUSES a join for a name that already has an attempt, anyone holding the shared join code can squat on classmates' names during the window — join as 'Alice' first and Alice cannot start her own attempt. This is strictly better than the behaviour it replaced (no data is read or altered, and the squatted attempt is visible in the teacher's report) but it is real, and there is currently NO teacher-side way to release an attempt. The natural follow-up is a 'release attempt' action on the report page. Left deliberately unfinished rather than inventing UI that was not requested.

FULL REPORT INGESTED AS A DOCUMENT (2026-09-11): the complete Rev 4 assessment — method, production context, every fixed finding with its verification evidence, the withdrawn SEC-12, the deployment-closed SEC-09, all 18 remaining findings with file:line anchors, the schema migrations, and the commit hashes — is stored in the document knowledge base as document_id 'simpleexam-security-audit' (filename simpleexam-security-audit.md, 33 chunks, format markdown). Retrieve it with the MCP retrieve tool scoped by that document_id. NOTE: use search_type 'semantic' — keyword/hybrid retrieval is currently broken on this server, see [[simplemcp-retrieve-keyword-broken]]. This entity holds the decisions and findings register; the document is the readable narrative.

entities.name: SimpleMCP
observations: Minimal PHP implementation of a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server
JSON-RPC 2.0 server exposing tools to MCP clients
Requires PHP >= 8.4
Runs in stdio mode or HTTP mode (php -S localhost:8000 index.php)
No test framework, linter, or CI configured
Uses json_validate(), match expressions, readonly classes, union types

Feature (2026-08-02): OAuth authorize login page offers 'Continue anonymously'. POSTing anonymous=1 to /oauth/authorize skips login and issues a code bound to the reserved UserStore::ANONYMOUS_USERNAME ('__anonymous__') identity; OAuthServer::resolveUser maps tokens carrying that username to UserContext::anonymous() (public tools only, no roles/permissions). The reserved username is rejected by onboarding (UserStore::onboardUser), so it can never collide with a real account. Client/redirect_uri/PKCE checks still apply to the anonymous grant.

HTTP mode adds: user context (every request tied to a UserContext resolved from an OAuth bearer token), per-tool access control (tools declare required roles/permissions; unauthorized tools are hidden from tools/list and rejected at tools/call with -32001), interactive OAuth 2.1 (Authorization Code + PKCE), and a user-management page (/account).
In stdio mode there is no HTTP user: every request runs as a trusted 'local' user with full access (UserContext::local()).
Running (stdio): php index.php — reads one JSON-RPC message per line on stdin, writes responses to stdout.

Running (HTTP): php -S localhost:8000 index.php — exposes OAuth + account endpoints plus the MCP JSON-RPC endpoint. Auth is optional: requests without a valid 'Authorization: Bearer' token run as an anonymous user who only sees/calls tools with no roles/permissions requirement; a present-but-invalid token is rejected with 401.
Manual smoke test (no test suite exists): pipe printf '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}\n{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}\n' into php index.php.

Gotcha: data/ is runtime-only and gitignored (/data/*): app.sqlite (users + tokens), memory.sqlite (memory tool graph + document store), sessions/. Deleting it re-seeds users from config/users.php on the next HTTP start. php -S ... index.php must be run with index.php as the router script so data/ is never served statically.
composer.json declares only php >= 8.4; the vendor/ tree also contains packages not listed there (phpdotenv, extendorm) that are unused leftovers.

observations: UMKM point-of-sale system for Indonesian small businesses
Backend: PHP with fishyboat21/simple-api per-file endpoint routing
Frontend: vanilla ES-module SPA + Bootstrap 5 CDN, no build step
Database: MySQL, auto-migrated from database/schema.sql and seeded from database/seed.sql on every boot
Run with php -S 127.0.0.1:8000 -t public/ ; default login admin/admin123
Features: POS terminal, dashboard, products+variants, categories, deductions, transactions, pending bills, users, roles, UMKM tax report

Product add/edit form now has a Stock input for non-variant products (id base-stock). It shows only when 'has variants' is off; toggling variants on hides it and stock comes from the variant table instead. On save, non-variant products send obj.stock = base-stock value (was previously always 0 — backend defaults products.stock to 0 when stock not sent). Layout row changed from 3x col-6 col-md-4 to 4x col-6 col-md-3 (Price/Cost/Category/Stock).

2026-08-08: added optional Stock by variant option (dimension mode) feature — per-option stock as source of truth, effective combination stock = MIN of options, sale decrements all constituent options. See [[stock-by-option-mode]].

GOTCHA (2026-08-08): Database::seed() runs on EVERY request (new PHP process per request under php -S), and seed.sql seeds Kaos Polos variant data with explicit IDs. Saving a variant product deletes+recreates its variant rows, so the next request re-seeds the old rows -> duplicate groups + POS 'Variant not found'. Fixed by latching @seed_kaos_polos in seed.sql so variant data is only bootstrapped when the product has no groups. See [[seed-reinsert-duplicate-bug]].
POS app in d:\Project\SimplePOS: PHP backend (fishyboat21/simple-api), vanilla ES module SPA, MySQL, Bootstrap 5
Admin login admin/admin123
database/seed.sql applied idempotently (INSERT IGNORE) on every boot via Database::getInstance()

2026-08-27: added customer management (CRUD + who-added-it tracking) and membership management (multi-tier, deduction-linked, auto-applied at checkout); POS binds bills to customers by phone with quick-add. See [[customer-membership-feature]], [[pos-model-customer]], [[pos-model-membership]].
2026-08-27: customers and memberships are seeded/managed through new endpoints /api/customers and /api/memberships with permissions 33-38; pending bills carry a customer through hold/resume/settle.

2026-08-27: schema repairs are now versioned — Database::patchSchema() only runs migrations the DB is behind on (SCHEMA_VERSION const + settings.schema_version marker); no more every-boot patch-all. See [[pos-decision-schema-versioning]].

2026-08-27: seed data is versioned like schema — Database::SEED_VERSION + settings.seed_version marker; seed.sql no longer re-runs on every request (one-time catch-up + version bumps only). See [[pos-decision-schema-versioning]].

2026-08-27: fixed products page header overflow — the 'Default stock mode' select + 'Add Product' button row (page-products template in public/index.html) could not wrap and overflowed on narrow screens. Header row and the right-hand control group now use d-flex flex-wrap with gap, the label is text-nowrap, and #default-stock-mode is capped at max-width:240px (matches the product form's #stock-mode-select, which already had max-width:240px). The page-products template renders the global default stock mode (settings key stock_mode_default, values 'combination'|'dimension') and is wired in app.js renderProductsPage() (api.settings.get/set, gated by products.write permission).

2026-08-27: fixed the 'default-stock-mode' (and product-form 'stock-mode-select') DROPDOWN overflow — a native select listbox sizes to the longest option's full text regardless of the 240px max-width on the closed control, so the long dimension-mode option poked past the right edge when opened. Shortened the option in both spots to 'By option (least of its options)' (index.html #default-stock-mode and app.js #stock-mode-select), which also removes the stray \' (escaped-quote) text bug — the option previously rendered as 'a combo\'s'. Product.php:143 still carries the full explanation in a comment ('sellable stock = the least of its options').

2026-08-27 (follow-up): the stock-mode dropdown still overflowed after the first shorten (32-char option) because a native <select> popup renders at the element's font size + its own padding and sizes to the longest option, which exceeded the max-width:240px cap on the CLOSED control (the cap clips the control but the popup ignores it, poking past the right edge near justify-content-between). Reduced the option to 28 chars ('By option (least of options)') in BOTH #default-stock-mode (index.html) and #stock-mode-select (app.js) so the open popup stays under 240px, and added a title tooltip carrying the full explanation ('Stock per combination, or per option (a combination's stock = the least of its options)').

2026-08-27: fixed mobile 'page overall height' overflow by switching viewport-height units from vh to dvh (dynamic viewport height, tracks the mobile URL bar). Core fix: app.css now sets pos-router .d-flex.vh-100 { height:100vh !important; height:100dvh !important; } which controls #app-layout (and the login/loading screens) — must be !important to beat Bootstrap's .vh-100, and targets pos-router because templates are cloned into it (their #page-* template ids are NOT preserved as live ancestors). GOTCHA: the old selectors #page-authenticated .d-flex.vh-100 and #page-pos .d-flex.h-100 were DEAD CODE — they never matched after template cloning; #page-pos actually fills via Bootstrap h-100 (100%). Also converted to dvh (with vh fallback): mobile cart sheet 85dvh, mobile modal-body calc(100dvh - 220px), cart items list max-height calc(100dvh - 380px), pending-bills table 60dvh. No vw units existed in the app so dvw was not needed.

2026-09-19: Timezone configured via .env (TIMEZONE=Asia/Jakarta). Database timestamps are set explicitly by PHP backend (date('Y-m-d H:i:s')) rather than DB functions. Frontend formatDate() displays datetimes directly without timezone conversion.

2026-09-20: Fixed thermal printed receipt transaction time wrong timezone bug in formatReceiptDate() \u2014 stopped treating database local timestamps as UTC (was previously appending 'Z' to datetime strings), now parses year/month/day/hour/minute/second directly matching app.js formatDate(). Also updated pos-waste.js fmtDate() to avoid '+ Z' offset shifts.

entities.name: SimplePOS / SimpleERP separation plan
observations: Principle (2026-08): front-of-house transactional core stays in SimplePOS (terminal, bills, transactions); back-of-house master data, inventory, production, finance move to SimpleERP.

Integration model: SimpleERP is the owner of domain tables (products, variants, ingredients, recipes, stock, customers, memberships, waste, production, purchasing). SimplePOS keeps its own transactional tables (transactions, bills) and reads/writes ERP domain data over the same MySQL server (cross-database or shared DB) — consistent with existing qclog/simplepos/ptku coexisting on one MariaDB. API option reserved as a later refactor.

Shared infrastructure (Database singleton, Auth + 2FA, AuthMiddleware, Mailer, exceptions, versioned migration runner, RBAC/seed) is COPIED per-project, not shared — established sibling-project pattern (QC Log, SimpleExam).

Phases: P0 copy skeleton + versioned migrations + RBAC; P1 move master data + customers/memberships; P2 inventory (ingredients, stock, waste) + recipes/production; P3 purchasing + suppliers; P4 reporting/finance consolidation.
POS keeps quick customer-bind + product lookup by reading ERP data; ERP owns all writes to domain tables.

CORRECTION (2026-08-27): integration model is now FULL SEPARATION + API — SimpleERP gets its OWN database (simpleerp) and own codebase/repo, no shared tables with SimplePOS. This SUPERSEDES the earlier 'same MySQL server / cross-database or shared DB / API as later refactor' note.
Implication: every cross-system read/write becomes an HTTP call — coupling moves from shared tables + FKs to an API contract + idempotency + failure handling.
SimplePOS keeps its own transactional tables (transactions, bills) and its own cashier auth; it talks to SimpleERP only over HTTP.

entities.name: SimplePOS Security Audit (2026-09-17)
observations: 2026-09-17: Comprehensive production-ready security audit of SimplePOS across authentication, authorization/RBAC, input validation/XSS, financial/stock transaction integrity, configuration & environment hardening, and Apache deployment.

Key vulnerabilities identified: Plaintext token storage in auth_tokens, flawed OTP brute-force rate limiting (counts issued codes not failed attempts), absence of login throttling, predictable device fingerprinting bypassing 2FA, missing settings permissions check on PUT /api/settings, unescaped innerHTML in pos-data-table.js and pos-sales-report.js causing Stored XSS, unit_price client tampering in checkout/bills, and missing Apache FastCGI Authorization header forwarding in .htaccess.

2026-09-17: High-priority security vulnerabilities resolved and verified. SEC-01: HTML escaping applied to pos-data-table.js, pos-sales-report.js, pos-waste.js to prevent Stored XSS. SEC-02: Transaction::resolveLine strictly enforces server-side catalog pricing and rejects client tampering. SEC-03 & SEC-04: OTP verification tracks failed attempts up to 5 max before invalidating the code; device trust relies on persistent crypto UUIDs in pos_device_id. SEC-05: Auth tokens stored as SHA-256 hashes in auth_tokens table. SEC-06: settings.read and settings.write permissions enforced on /api/settings endpoints.

2026-09-17: Committed high-priority security fixes in commit 853abe7: resolved SEC-01 (Stored XSS), SEC-02 (price tampering), SEC-03 (OTP rate limiting), SEC-04 (device ID UUID), SEC-05 (token SHA-256 hashing), and SEC-06 (settings RBAC). Database schema bumped to version 5.

entities.name: SimplePOS stays: Terminal
observations: POS terminal: cart, checkout, payment methods, receipts — STAYS in SimplePOS.

With the API-separation decision (2026-08-27): SimplePOS gains a small HTTP API client for SimpleERP (catalog + stock + customer lookups, stock consumption, sales push) instead of direct DB access to ERP-owned tables.

POS-side design considerations to decide: sale-time latency/offline degradation, local cache vs real-time reads, idempotency keys for writes, who computes checkout totals (recommendation: keep in POS, source membership deduction from ERP).

entities.name: StirlingPdfClient
observations: Client for a Stirling-PDF server in src/StirlingPdfClient.php — final, no deps beyond PHP streams (file_get_contents + hand-built multipart body, field fileInput; needs allow_url_fopen, no cURL)

Endpoints: POST /api/v1/convert/markdown/pdf (returns PDF bytes, must start with %PDF) and /api/v1/convert/pdf/markdown (returns extracted Markdown; empty body → 'no extractable text layer' error). Optional X-API-KEY header. 60s timeout, 100MB input cap

forUser(?UserContext) resolves settings transport-aware: stdio (PHP_SAPI==='cli') → global config/config.php as-is; HTTP with a username → per-account SettingsStore keys stirling_pdf_endpoint/stirling_pdf_api_key, blank fields fall back to the global defaults

Guards: configurationError() (empty or non-http(s) endpoint) checked before every call — remains as a defensive fallback even though PdfTool::isAvailable() now disables the tools before they can be called

Added convertImageToPdf() and convertPdfToImage() in src/StirlingPdfClient.php. Targets POST /api/v1/convert/img/pdf and POST /api/v1/convert/pdf/img. Updated postFile() to accept optional extraFields for multipart form data (fitOption, colorType, autoRotate, imageFormat, singleOrMultiple, pageNumbers, dpi).

convertPdfToImage detects multi-page output by ZIP magic bytes (str_starts_with($body, "PK\x03\x04")) and switches the extension/mimeType to zip/application/zip; the result carries isZip, imageFormat, filename (via outputName()) and endpoint.

postFile() is now postFile($path, $filename, $contentType, $content, array $extraFields = []): extra fields are emitted as multipart parts before the fileInput part, and null/'' values are skipped so Stirling-PDF's own defaults apply. autoRotate is always sent, as 'true'/'false'.

convertImageToPdf maps the upload's extension to a Content-Type (png/jpg/jpeg/webp/gif/bmp/tiff/tif/svg → image/*, default application/octet-stream) and validates the response begins with %PDF within its first 1024 bytes before returning ok.

entities.name: Stock by variant option (dimension mode)
observations: Optional per-product stock mode for variant products, added 2026-08-08 as an extra that coexists with the existing per-combination stock
products.stock_mode column: 'combination' (existing default, per-combination product_variants.stock) vs 'dimension' (new, per-option variant_options.stock as source of truth)

In dimension mode the effective sellable stock of any combination = MIN of its constituent option stocks (e.g. Flavor Orange=10 x Size Large=5 -> Orange/Large=5); blank/unset option stock counts as 0 (strict min)

A sale in dimension mode decrements EVERY constituent option (selling Orange/Large consumes one Orange and one Large cup), which lowers other combinations sharing those options; decrement pre-checks all options >= qty and runs inside the caller's DB transaction so partial decrements roll back on shortfall

product_variants.stock stays materialized as MIN-of-options via recomputeDimensionStocks() so all existing readers (POS selector, cart, checkout, Transaction/Bill deduction) work unchanged; products.stock re-summed via syncProductStock()
recomputeDimensionStocks uses a single UPDATE with a LEFT JOIN derived MIN table, then syncs parent product stock; helper variantStockMode()/variantOptionIds() branch the decrement/increment paths
Frontend: per-option stock inputs (.vo-stock) in the variant-groups editor render only in dimension mode; the generated variants table omits its Stock column in dimension mode
MAX-backfill guardrail: switching a product combination->dimension prefills each option's stock with MAX of the existing combinations' stocks so no live combination silently drops to 0 stock

Global default: new settings table (skey/svalue key-value) + public/api/settings.php endpoint (GET products.read / PUT products.write, INSERT..ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE) store 'stock_mode_default'; new products default to it, existing products keep their own stock_mode override
obj.stock is sent as 0 for dimension products on save — the backend recomputes the true MIN-based stock (comment in app.js)

entities.name: Transaction model
observations: App\Models\Transaction in src/Models/Transaction.php
create() runs a DB transaction: resolves lines, computeTotals(), inserts transaction/items/deductions, reserves stock
computeTotals() is a pure deduction pipeline: manual deductions first (running reduced base), then system/tax on subtotal − manual discounts
void() restores stock for ACTIVE lines only, sets status='voided' + voided_by/at/reason audit columns; pending bills may only be voided via Bill::cancel
generateInvoiceNumber() → INV-{Ymd}-{seq} walking past collisions; getStats() → today/week/month revenue, top products, daily sales for the dashboard
resolveLine() appends the variant label to the product name and picks the variant price

Transaction::create() and resolveLine() capture product_name + unit_price per line but do NOT snapshot unit_cost; adding a unit_cost column to transaction_items (populated in resolveLine from variant/plain cost) is the minimal prerequisite for a correct COGS-based profit/loss report.

Transaction::create(items, deduction_ids, payment_*) inserts the transactions row, reserves stock per line (Product::decreaseStock/decreaseVariantStock), snapshots applied deductions into transaction_deductions, then returns Transaction::find(id) with 'deductions' attached

computeTotals(items, manualIds) is the pure deduction pipeline: manual deductions applied to the running base (subtotal minus earlier manual discounts), then system deductions (tax) on the taxable base; returns subtotal/discount/tax/grand_total/applied_deductions
A pending bill is just a transactions row with status='pending' (Bill model operates on it); Transaction::void rejects pending unless allowPending=true
generateInvoiceNumber(): INV-{Ymd}-{seq}, walks past taken numbers (reserved by pending bills)

2026-08-27 customer/membership: computeTotals(array $items, array $manualIds = [], ?int $customerId = null) resolves the bound customer's ACTIVE membership deduction via Customer::membershipDeduction() and applies it FIRST on the full subtotal (running base), then the cashier-selected manual deductions, then system tax — the same order the POS cart previews, so the screen total always equals the settled one.
The membership deduction id is filtered out of manualIds so a cashier selecting the same deduction never double-applies it; the applied-deduction snapshot entry is tagged 'is_membership' => true.

all()/find() LEFT JOIN customers c, memberships m, deductions md to expose customer_name, customer_phone, customer_membership_id, membership_name, membership_deduction_{id,name,method,value,is_active}.
create() reads $data['customer_id'] (int or null), inserts it into transactions, and passes it to computeTotals.

Transaction::all() currently has a hardcoded LIMIT 100 and does not attach line items. Transaction::paginate() is needed to support server-side pagination (page, per_page, total count) and batch-load transaction_items and transaction_deductions so transactions list can display all items without N+1 queries.
computeTotals supports passing payment method so customer-paid service fee is computed on net subtotal and incorporated into the tax calculation base before determining grand_total

Transaction::create caught \Exception and previously re-threw \RuntimeException(..., 500), which masked ValidationException from reserveItemStock and caused 500 Internal Server Error instead of 400 ValidationException on stock shortfall. Preserve HttpException instances to return 400 Bad Request.

entities.name: Uncached Relations and N+1 Query Problem
observations: Model::__get() executes a new database query on every property access without memoizing the result on the model instance
Repeated access to '$post->author' runs duplicate queries; iterating over a collection triggers N+1 database roundtrips with no eager-loading ('with()') support

FIXED (2026-09-13): Model::__construct() unsets declared relation properties so PHP 8+ __get() can intercept access; Model::__get() memoizes results on $this->loadedRelations, preventing redundant N+1 queries on the same model instance.

entities.name: Unescaped SQL Identifiers and Reserved Words
observations: QueryBuilder2 and Model do not quote table or column identifiers (no backticks or double quotes)
Queries fail when table or column names match SQL reserved keywords (e.g., 'order', 'group', 'user', 'status', 'key')
Columns interpolated directly into WHERE and ORDER BY clauses without whitelist validation or quoting present SQL injection risks if column names are user-controlled

entities.name: Uninitialized Typed Primary Key Crash
observations: In Model::Save(), checking 'if ($this->$primaryKey != null)' attempts to read the property value before initialization
In PHP 8.0+, accessing an uninitialized typed property (e.g. 'public int $id;') throws a fatal Error instead of returning null; requires isset() or ?int $id = null
In Model::Delete(), setting '$this->$primaryKey = null;' on a non-nullable typed int property throws a TypeError

FIXED (2026-09-13): Model::Save() now uses 'isset($this->$primaryKey) && $this->$primaryKey !== null' allowing uninitialized typed properties to safely branch to insert. GetValues() uses 'isset($this->$prop) ? $this->$prop : null'. Model::Delete() resets PK using 'try { $this->$primaryKey = null; } catch (\\TypeError) { unset($this->$primaryKey); }', safely supporting non-nullable typed properties.

entities.name: Variant seed delete/recreate gotcha
observations: Editing seed product 16 'Kaos Polos' through the variant delete-then-recreate flow accumulates duplicate variant_groups/variant_options across restarts

Cause: Database::seed() re-inserts seed rows (INSERT IGNORE) on every boot; canonical seed groups/options (ids 1,2 / 1-5) come back, but canonical seed variants (ids 1-6, KP-* SKUs) CANNOT be re-inserted once a recreated row holds a KP-* SKU (unique constraint)
Practical effect: after editing seed variant products, next boot re-adds stale empty groups — don't edit seed products' variants in place, or re-seed to recover

entities.name: Versioned schema migrations
observations: 2026-08-20: SimpleExam switches Schema::patch() from unversioned idempotent guards to a versioned migration runner to fix PER-REQUEST PATCHING COST - the old patch() ran ~10 information_schema SELECT guards plus ~13 DDL/DML statements on EVERY request (page load or cron) even when the schema was current (~23 DB ops/request just to 'check').

Design: Schema::VERSION const + schema_versions table (version INT PK, applied_at); patch() reads MAX(version) - one indexed read on the happy path - and only runs numbered migrations 1..VERSION the DB is behind on, recording each. Static in-process cache so it runs once per request. Migrations stay idempotent via 'needs' guards (re-run safe after failure); a failed SQL is logged and not recorded (retried next boot).

User rejected a CLI tool and a dashboard banner (2026-08-20, 4 plan iterations) - the deliverable is the migration SQL logged via error_log('Schema: applied migration N (reason): <sql>') plus auto-apply gated on the version. README documents the scheme; setup.php seeds schema_versions for fresh installs (only when answers.drawing_json exists, so a re-install over an older DB is left unseeded and migrates up instead).

Perf win verified: real dev DB on the fast path logs no migrations and does 1 query; a scratch DB behind all migrations applied v2-v17 in order (v1 skipped - attempt_minutes pre-existed) and all 17 checks passed. See [[se-schema]].

entities.name: Versioned schema migrations
observations: 2026-08-27: SimplePOS switches Database::patchSchema() from an unversioned every-boot patch-all (~35 DB ops/request) to a versioned migration runner to fix per-request patching cost.

Design: Database::SCHEMA_VERSION const + MIGRATIONS map (version => method name); applied version recorded in the settings table (skey 'schema_version'); patchSchema() reads it (one indexed read on the happy path), runs only the migrations the DB is behind on in order, recording after each success; a failed migration is logged and retried on the next boot (marker stays at last completed version); a failure never breaks boot.

Existing installs (no marker = version 0) run migration 1 = the old cumulative patch set (fully idempotent ensureX guards), then record version 1 — a one-time catch-up. Fresh installs reach the same state via database/schema.sql.

Adapted from SimpleExam's versioned Schema::patch() [[se-decision-schema-versioning]]; the version is stored in the existing settings k/v table rather than a dedicated schema_versions table, matching SimplePOS's existing one-time-marker convention (cost_components_backfilled_v2).
Verified on the dev DB 2026-08-27: first boot applies migration 1 and records version 1; a second fresh boot does zero patch work (happy path = 1 read).

2026-08-27: the same versioned pattern was extended to seed data — SEED_VERSION const + settings.seed_version marker; seed() skips the heavy INSERT IGNORE pass when current, running only on a version bump (verified on the dev DB: first boot applies + records version 1, second boot does zero seed work).

entities.name: pos-cart
observations: Light-DOM cart in pos-cart.js; live totals, deduction checkboxes, payment method/amount
Bill mode: banner shows the pending invoice, +/- dispatch pos-bill-add-item, Remove dispatches a supervisor-gated void request
checkout() settles the bill or creates a transaction, then dispatches pos-show-receipt and refreshes product grid + data tables
updateTotalsDisplay() mirrors the backend's running-base deduction calculation
Cart panel is Light-DOM custom element; in bill mode mirrors the server bill via pos-bill-synced events and dispatches pos-bill-add-item/pos-bill-void-request
checkout() calls api.bills.settle (bill mode) or api.transactions.create (normal), passing payment_method, payment_amount, deduction_ids; then clears cart and fires pos-show-receipt
Real-time totals preview: loadDeductions() renders manual-deduction checkboxes; updateTotalsDisplay() recomputes manual discount (running base) + system tax matching backend Deduction::calculate

2026-08-27 customer/membership: customer section under the header — when a customer is bound show name/phone/membership badge + Remove (clear-customer-btn nulls cart.customer); otherwise a phone input + Bind button with Enter-key support.
Dispatches pos-customer-bind-request with { phone }; the app resolves the customer (exact match / picker / quick-add) and binds via Store.
applyBill() restores cart.customer from the authoritative bill payload (id/name/phone/membership_name/membership_deduction) so a bill sync keeps the member.
checkout() sends customer_id (cart.customer?.id ?? null) on both api.bills.settle and api.transactions.create.

updateTotalsDisplay() applies cart.customer.membership_deduction FIRST on the full subtotal (mirroring Transaction::computeTotals), shows a 'Member discount (<name>)' line, and skips the member's deduction id in the manual loop.

2026-08-27: breakdown & deduction section made foldable — the member-discount row, manual-deduction checkboxes, discount row, and tax row are wrapped in #details-collapse, toggled by a 'Deductions & breakdown' button (chevron up/down). Subtotal and Total rows stay always visible; default state is collapsed.
Foldable state lives on the component instance (_detailsOpen), so it survives the full re-renders triggered on every cart change; clicking the toggle flips it and calls render().

updateDetailsToggleVisibility() hides the toggle entirely when there is nothing to fold (no member deduction, no active manual/system deductions) — called on render and again after loadDeductions() resolves so it appears once deduction data arrives.

2026-08-27: fixed 'Totals & Checkout section blocking cart items'. The cart panel flex layout was fragile: cart-items-list carried a brittle inline max-height:calc(100dvh - 380px) that assumed header+customer+totals is about 380px (now taller with the foldable deductions section + payment + action buttons), so on height-bound screens the totals section could squeeze/overlap the list. Fix: removed the max-height inline cap; the list now uses flex-grow-1 + overflow-auto + min-height:0 so it scrolls to exactly the leftover space; the bill banner, cart header, customer section, and Totals & Checkout all got flex-shrink-0 so they never get squeezed over the list; pos-cart element got overflow-hidden to clip residual bleed. The mobile media rule 'pos-cart .cart-items-list { max-height: none !important }' is now redundant but harmless (no inline max-height to override).

2026-08-27 (follow-up): cart still squeezed/overflowed when adding items or expanding the breakdown. Two more fixes: (1) pos-cart now gets an explicit bounded height in app.css base rule — pos-cart { height:100vh; height:100dvh; } — so adding items scrolls the list instead of growing the panel regardless of the flex-chain (mobile still overrides to the fixed 85dvh bottom sheet in the media query); (2) the foldable #details-collapse is capped at max-height:20vh/20dvh with overflow-y:auto, so expanding the 'Deductions & breakdown' toggle scrolls internally instead of squeezing the cart item list out of view. Item list carries flex-basis:0 + min-height:0 + flex-grow-1 + overflow-auto so it takes exactly the leftover space.

2026-08-27: POS cart secondary action buttons (Hold Bill, Pending Bills, Clear Cart) changed from 1-per-row (each w-100 mt-2 stacked) to 2-per-row using a d-flex flex-wrap gap-2 row with each button flex:0 0 calc(50% - 0.25rem) so exactly two share each row and an odd third stays half-width. The primary checkout button (Complete Sale / Settle Bill) stays full-width. Bill-mode's single Pending Bills button and the empty-cart case are unchanged.

2026-08-27: payment method + amount received are now hidden behind the checkout button. The Payment Method select and Amount Received input live inside a #payment-section div that starts d-none. First click of the primary button (Complete Sale / Settle Bill) sets _paymentShown=true, re-renders to reveal the fields, retitles the button to 'Pay Now' / 'Confirm Payment', and focuses the amount input; the second click runs checkout(). Reveal state (_paymentShown) lives on the component instance so it survives the full re-renders on every cart change; render() resets it to false whenever the cart is empty and checkout() resets it in the success path before Store.clearCart().
Payment section currently has hardcoded cash/card/transfer select and amount received input. Settle and checkout send payment_method to backend. Needs dynamic payment methods with MDR fee support.

2026-09-13: Fixed Clear Cart button not working. The clear button previously relied on native window.confirm(), which was silently blocked/auto-dismissed in Chromium/browsers when DevTools or dialog suppression is active. Replaced with an in-app <pos-modal> confirmation dialog ('Clear Cart' with Cancel and Clear Cart action buttons) that calls Store.clearCart() and shows a toast notification.

2026-09-10: verified the buy-packs card is fully config-driven — it iterates Credits::packs() (config app.credit_packs) and computes the 'Save {percent}% vs single' badge from the 'single' pack's per-credit price, so the 2026-09-10 price change (1 credit / Rp 2.000, 20 credits / Rp 10.000) renders as 'Save 75% vs single' with no code change in this file.
COSMETIC (pre-existing): the pack row label is literally `<?= $pid ?> credits`, so the 1-credit pack renders as '1 credits'.

SECURITY REVIEW 2026-09-10 (finding verified, code-accuracy lens): the POST purchase handler (public_html/credits.php:25-74) has NO throttle, NO pending-order cap, and NO reuse of an existing pending order. Every POST with a valid pack key does a fresh INSERT INTO credit_orders (lines 47-51, status hardcoded 'pending'), commits (line 54), then calls Doku::createPayment (line 60) which performs a real outbound HTTPS request via file_get_contents (src/Doku.php sendSigned ~line 213). Csrf::verify() (line 26) is the only gate and the token is per-session-never-rotated (src/Csrf.php:11-16), so a logged-in teacher can script unlimited requests. Credits::packs() keys are 'single'/'bulk20' per config.php app.credit_packs. No unique key constrains pending orders (src/Schema.php:272-289 has UNIQUE only on invoice_number; idx_co_user_status is non-unique).

The invoice number is derived from the auto-increment id: 'SE-' . $orderId (public_html/credits.php:53), so order ids are sequential and leak into every invoice_number (SE-<id>) shown in the order-history table (line 207) — enumerable by an attacker who owns any account. payment_return.php is a further amplifier: a GET visit to payment_return.php?order=<own pending id> is deliberately NOT CSRF-gated (payment_return.php:20-22,32-34) and calls Doku::checkStatus (line 50) on every visit while the order stays 'pending'; it is scoped to the caller's own order (lines 36-43), so the account-farming premise supplies the ids. Reachability confirmed: Bootstrap does not gate on app.installed (only setup.php reads it), and the committed config.php has app.registration_open=true (line 54) with real doku.client_id (line 91), so both the outbound call path and the account-farming premise hold.

entities.name: public_html/doku_notify.php
observations: Public DOKU payment-notification webhook, NO PHP session — uses the lightweight bootstrap (config + timezone + helpers + Schema::patch), mirroring cron_finalize.php.

Verifies the notification signature (401 + error_log on mismatch), grants idempotently via `UPDATE credit_orders SET status='paid', paid_at=NOW() WHERE id=? AND status='pending'` (rowCount==1 → Credits::adjust(+credits,'purchase')), and always acks 2xx promptly. FAILED/CANCELLED/EXPIRE/DECLINED flips a pending order to failed.
Deployment: the notify URL must be reachable over public HTTPS (app.base_url) and its server IP whitelisted in DOKU Back Office.

Verified against DOKU notification best-practice docs (2026-09-04): transaction.status is only 'SUCCESS'|'FAILED', and for Checkout integrations FAILED must be IGNORED (the customer can retry on the checkout page and succeed) — so doku_notify.php no longer marks an order failed on FAILED/CANCELLED/EXPIRE/DECLINED; it only grants on SUCCESS and acks 2xx otherwise. Also confirmed the signature Request-Target = path of the notify URL (/doku_notify.php), which verifyNotification() already computes from REQUEST_URI. Non-strict JSON parse (ignore unknown fields) and idempotent handling (mark-paid guarded by status='pending') already match the documented best practice.

2026-09-04: the webhook's SUCCESS grant now delegates to Credits::grantOrder(id) (shared with payment_return.php) instead of its own inline guarded UPDATE+adjust; a replayed/racing notification returns false (no-op) and is acked 2xx, only a real grant failure returns 500. entities.name: retrieve() keyword/hybrid search returns non-matching chunks — use search_type semantic
observations: OBSERVED 2026-09-11: the MCP retrieve tool's keyword (BM25/FTS5) ranking does not appear to be working over ingested documents. Retrieving the exact token SUBMIT_LATE_TOLERANCE_SECONDS — a string occurring exactly once, inside chunk #13 of the document simpleexam-security-audit — returned chunks #5, #31 and #3 under search_type 'keyword', NONE of which contain the token. Every hit reported matchedOn: [] and near-identical scores (0.0161-0.0167) regardless of the query, which is the signature of arbitrary ordering rather than relevance.

WORKAROUND THAT WORKS: search_type 'semantic' (n-gram similarity) DOES retrieve by content. The same query returned chunk #13 — the chunk containing the token — with matchedOn: ['content']. Because 'hybrid' fuses keyword + semantic via RRF, it inherits the broken half and also misses; so on this server, retrieving from the document KB should use search_type 'semantic' explicitly rather than relying on the default.
document_id scoping is NOT affected — passing document_id correctly restricts results to that document. Only the ranking/matching within the candidate set is wrong.

NOT YET DIAGNOSED: whether this is a missing/stale FTS index for newly ingested documents, a tokenizer issue, or a bug in the fusion/ranking code. Likely worth investigating in the SimpleMCP repo (ingest_document / the FTS5 index build) — a unique-token query failing to find its own chunk is a strong, cheap regression test to add.

Practical impact: a freshly ingested document is addressable and readable by document_id, and findable via semantic search, but NOT findable via the default hybrid search. Anyone concluding 'the ingestion did not work' from a hybrid query would be wrong.

RESOLVED 2026-09-11 — root cause confirmed and fixed. The 'keyword/hybrid returns non-matching chunks' symptom was an INVERTED FTS5 rank sort, not a stale index or a tokenizer crash. SQLite FTS5's hidden `rank` column is a NEGATED BM25 score (better match = numerically smaller value), so best-first ordering is `ORDER BY rank` ASC. Both DocumentStore::keywordSearch (src/Auth/DocumentStore.php:477) and MemoryStore::keywordSearch (src/Auth/MemoryStore.php:1477) used `ORDER BY rank DESC`, surfacing the worst matches at the top and pushing the best (chunk #13, rank -18.71) to the bottom — exactly the observed 'arbitrary ordering, matchedOn []' signature. Fix: DESC -> ASC in both files (one-line each, + explanatory comment), uncommitted on branch feat/main_MyRAG. Verified through the real DocumentStore/MemoryStore classes: `retrieve(..., 'keyword', 5)` and `searchGraph(..., 'keyword', 5, 0)` now rank the token-containing chunk/entity first with matchedOn ['content']. The workaround (use search_type semantic) is no longer required once the server is restarted to pick up the patch.

REMAINING OPEN ISSUE after this fix: identifier tokenization. FTS5 unicode61 indexes `submit_late_tolerance_seconds` as a single token (underscore is an identifier char), while ftsMatchQuery() splits the query on underscores into prefix-OR terms — exact-token recall for underscore-containing identifiers is still imperfect (a mid-token substring is un-indexable). Distinct from the sort defect; tracked separately.

Fix committed 2026-09-11 as e02ee28 'Fix inverted FTS5 rank sort in keyword search' on branch feat/main_MyRAG (working tree clean; 2 files changed: src/Auth/DocumentStore.php + src/Auth/MemoryStore.php). Server restart still required for the running MCP process to pick it up.

2026-09-12 PROBED IN DETAIL (post-fix, live server): the underscore-tokenizer gap is narrower than the worst case suggested. (1) unicode61 DOES index the whole underscored identifier as one token (submit_late_tolerance_seconds), and the split-term prefix-OR query recovered chunk #13 under keyword/hybrid for BOTH the full-identifier query AND the tail-only query LATE_TOLERANCE_SECONDS — because 'submit' 'late' 'tolerance' also appear as standalone prose words in the same chunk, so the split terms happened to hit. (2) The unsplit whole-run term "submit_late_tolerance_seconds"* hits exactly chunk #13 alone (precision 1/1). (3) The genuine recall gap: a NON-head segment that never appears as a standalone prose word. On the real corpus, "grace" exists only inside submit_grace_seconds, and GRACE_SECONDS found #13 via 'grace' alone; but in a synthetic doc where MAX_LATE_SECONDS appears ONLY as the identifier (no supporting prose), the query LATE_SECONDS returned rows via 'late'/'seconds' prose hits — row recall still worked because one of the tail segments ('max') is also the head of the indexed token, and 'late'/'seconds' also appear in row 2's prose. The strictly unreachable case is a NON-head segment unique to the identifier while every split term's prose coincidences fail: then no split term prefix-matches the indexed token, and the whole identifier is only reachable via its head segment. Net: recall for head segments is guaranteed by the prefix star; tail segments ride prose coincidence; the identifier as a whole is reachable only when its head is quoted.

MEASURED SCOPE of the split (2 fixed FTS mirrors, 1 in-memory source each): memory_chunks_fts (85 chunks, 1 user) and memory_entities_fts (~376 entities' names+types+observations, incl. the 7-observation simplemcp-retrieve-keyword-broken entity). Fix candidates measured on the real corpus: (a) also adding the unsplit alnum run to the OR — for SUBMIT_LATE_TOLERANCE_SECONDS the head segment 'submit' prefix-hits the indexed token, so extra term adds precision but zero recall change; (b) CJK case verified separately: a whole Chinese run indexes as ONE token, so a query split on spaces fails ('知识 图谱' matched nothing) while the head chars '知识'* hit — meaning the semantic path (trigram) remains the reliable recall path for CJK, consistent with the code comments.

FIX DIRECTION if taken up: ftsMatchQuery() in both stores could emit BOTH the split terms AND the full alnum run ("max"* OR "late"* OR "seconds"* OR "max_late_seconds"*) — cheap, keeps recall guarantees for head segments, adds an exact whole-identifier signal for BM25 to weigh. Alternative: trigram tokenizer rebuild, much heavier, unnecessary given the semantic path already covers fuzzy/CJK recall. This is a precision/recall optimization, NOT a correctness bug like the inverted rank sort; keyword retrieval currently works for every probe thrown at it on the real corpus.

FIX IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-12 (working tree, uncommitted): the identifier-tokenizer gap in ftsMatchQuery() is closed in BOTH stores (src/Auth/DocumentStore.php:568-601, src/Auth/MemoryStore.php:1690-1726). The MATCH expression now ALSO emits each underscored run VERBATIM (underscores kept, lowercased) as an extra prefix term: SUBMIT_LATE_TOLERANCE_SECONDS now builds "submit"* OR "late"* OR "tolerance"* OR "seconds"* OR "submit_late_tolerance_seconds"*. New private wholeRuns() helper extracts the runs (split on everything except letters/digits/underscores, must contain an underscore AND at least one letter/digit, deduped). First patch attempt had a bug CAUGHT BY ITS OWN VERIFICATION: it split on \p{P} (which INCLUDES underscore) then stripped underscores from fragments that no longer had any — a no-op that produced identical MATCH output; fixed to split on [^\p{L}\p{N}_] and keep the run verbatim. Rationale documented in code comments + MemoryStore docblock.

VERIFIED post-fix through the real classes on the real corpus: full-identifier, tail-only (LATE_TOLERANCE_SECONDS), and single-word-tail (GRACE_SECONDS) queries all return chunk #13 first under keyword AND hybrid with matchedOn ['content']; attempt_secret ranks chunk #5 first; prose queries byte-identical to pre-fix ordering (['12','13','16'] / ['5','4','6']); degenerate queries ([], whitespace, '___', punctuation) short-circuit to total=0 via the existing empty-MATCH guard; a 100-identifier query builds 400 OR terms and executes fine. CJK underscore runs (数_字) also emit the whole-run term. Server restart required for the live MCP process to pick it up.

Supersedes the 'uncommitted' status noted earlier — the working tree is now clean. Server restart still required for the live MCP process to pick it up.

observations: public_html/session_delete.php — DELETE s JOIN exams for ownership
2026-08-11: captures exam_id via SELECT s.exam_id JOIN exams (ownership) before DELETE, then redirects to sessions.php?i=<exam_id> (falls back to dashboard.php if no valid row).

SECURITY REVIEW 2026-09-10 (adversarial verification, finding CONFIRMED as a real race; severity calibrated down from high to MEDIUM): the refund path at lines 26-42 is three separate non-transactional queries — COUNT attempts (26-28), EXISTS session_create ledger row (29-33), DELETE session (35-38) — and the refund at line 40-42 tests the PRE-DELETE values ($attemptCount === 0 && $wasCharged) with NO $del->rowCount() check and NO transaction wrapping. Two concurrent POSTs from two PHP sessions of the same teacher (remember-me makes two live browser sessions easy; PHP session-file locking only serializes requests sharing one cookie) can both read attemptCount=0 + wasCharged=true before either DELETE lands; the loser's DELETE affects 0 rows but still refunds, so Credits::adjust(+1,'session_refund',$id) fires twice for one session. Net per won race: create session (-1) then race-delete (x2) = +1 credit. Verified credits_transactions has no UNIQUE on (reference_id, reason) — only PRIMARY KEY(id) + non-unique KEYs (src/Schema.php:255-270) — and no consumed/refunded flag on the session_create row, so nothing prevents the second refund. Exploitability: attacker is the AUTHENTICATED account owner (Auth::requireTeacher), zero-risk (a lost race refunds once, net 0, no loss), repeatable but requires winning a narrow TOCTOU window (~two SELECTs) per cycle; gain = 1 credit = Rp 2.000 (config.php credit_packs single), i.e. revenue bypass on the only paid feature — no data, login, or DoS impact, and the duplicate (session_refund, reference_id) pairs are visible in the ledger and reversible by the operator. Same non-transactional refund pattern exists in exam_delete.php:19-33 (collect refundSessionIds then delete then refund loop), which additionally races with session_delete on the SAME session.

entities.name: setup.php install lock never engages (permanent unauthenticated installer)
observations: SECURITY REVIEW 2026-09-10 (exploitability & impact calibration lens): VERIFIED, not refuted. Severity critical (as shipped).

Mechanism confirmed: app.installed is READ ONLY. grep across the repo for 'installed' returns exactly config.php:26 ('installed' => false), public_html/setup.php:7 (read), setup.php:12 (the lock branch), setup.php:299 (comment), src/Schema.php:8 (comment). NO code path anywhere writes it; nothing writes config.php. So the production lock at setup.php:12 can never engage while the shipped config hard-codes false.

Reachability confirmed: /setup.php is not denied by .htaccess (root .htaccess denies config.php/composer/README/CLAUDE.md and src|vendor|.git dirs; public_html/.htaccess only blocks logs) and the root rewrite sends /setup.php -> public_html/setup.php. No auth gate, no install token.

Admin identity: setup.php:280-294 promotes (UPDATE users SET role='admin' WHERE email=?) or, when adminCount===0, INSERTs the account for the hard-coded Config app.admin_email (config.php:57 = tembok511@gmail.com) and grants the signup bonus. multilang.json:373-374 renders 'setup.admin_created'/'setup.admin_present' with {email} into the success alert (setup.php:331-333), so GET /setup.php echoes the admin email to any anonymous caller.

Takeover step rides on a SEPARATE weakness, not on setup.php itself: config.php:106 smtp.host='' -> Mailer::sendLoginOtp() returns false (src/Mailer.php:16-19) -> Otp::issue() takes the demo branch and Flash::set('warning', otp.flash_demo with the plaintext code) (src/Otp.php:57-63); View::renderFlashes() echoes the flash raw (src/View.php:112-127) on the next page load (verify.php). So POST login.php with the leaked admin email -> the 6-digit code is displayed on verify.php -> POST it -> Auth::login(). Confirmed the whole chain in login.php:22-36 and verify.php:22-46.

Impact if admin is obtained: Auth::requireAdmin() gates users.php (credit adjust admin_adjust, create/delete users, mark DOKU orders paid) and user_delete.php; admin also sees/manages every teacher's exams, sessions, attempts and graded answers (exam-answer theft, credit/monetisation abuse, mass data exposure). Genuine, not cosmetic.

Honest calibration note: the finding's title attributes the takeover to setup.php, but setup.php only guarantees + PUBLISHES the fixed admin identity; the credential-free login itself comes from the OTP demo-mode fallback. If smtp.host is configured (operator sets it), the takeover path closes and setup.php alone degrades to an admin-email info leak + on-demand admin re-creation (medium). As shipped (host=''), the composite is unauthenticated remote admin takeover = critical.

No existing mitigation reduces it: RateLimit is session-scoped (bypassable with a fresh cookie), Csrf::verify() is per-session (a fresh GET yields a valid token), Bootstrap::run() has no install check or global throttle.

Remediation: write app.installed=true (or a sentinel file) from setup.php after success; ship config.php with installed=true and require an out-of-band setup token; deny /setup.php in .htaccess once installed.

App\View (src/View.php) — the shared HTML layout for SimpleExam. renderStart($title, $user) emits doctype/head/navbar (+flash alerts) and renderEnd() closes the container and loads the Bootstrap JS bundle; pages call them around their own markup.

~17 pages render through it — every teacher/app page (dashboard, questions, exams, sessions, report, attempt_view, users, credits, setup) plus the public login/register/verify and the student take.php.

Navbar is Bootstrap 'navbar navbar-expand-md navbar-dark bg-primary'; the brand is a plain text link to dashboard.php (logged in) or index.php (guest) — no logo image. The collapse holds the language <select> (window.setLang) and, when logged in, the Users (admin) / Credits / Logout actions.

2026-09-10: <head> now links the site icon set from public_html/assets — favicon.ico (sizes=any), icon.svg, favicon-32x32.png, favicon-16x16.png, apple-touch-icon (180x180), site.webmanifest — plus <meta name="theme-color" content="#4F46E5">. This single edit gives every View-rendered page its favicon; the landing page public_html/home.php has its own <head> and carries its own copy of the tags.
Asset refs inside the layout are relative (assets/app.css, assets/icon.svg) while home.php uses root-absolute (/assets/...) — both resolve at the docroot root.

2026-08-16 BUG FIX: auto-submit at time-up crashed with 'form.submit is not a function' whenever the countdown hit 0 on the LAST question. Root cause: the final Submit button was <button name="submit">, and per the HTML named-getter rule a form control named 'submit' shadows the native HTMLFormElement.prototype.submit method, so form.submit() in autoSubmit() resolved to the button element. The button only renders when pos >= total, which is why the crash was specific to time-up on the last question. Fixed by renaming the button to name="final" and the server's final-submit check to isset($_POST['final']) (was $_POST['submit']) — the timeout=1 path is unchanged.

2026-08-16 hardening: autoSubmit() now calls HTMLFormElement.prototype.submit.call(form) instead of form.submit() — immune to a form control named/id'd "submit" shadowing the native method, so no future button rename can break the forced time-up submit again. Note: this only affects newly-served pages; an exam tab already open before the fix still runs the old JS until reloaded (resume is safe — in_progress attempts restore at last saved question).
